deployment_linkage: Weakly present: the second-project procedure note's 'CI/Makefile parity scan' (Sec.11.1) touches CI/build-pipeline concerns, but the architecture does not model a distinct deployment/runtime-observation stage beyond task completion and its packetized recovery/rollback.
runtime_observation_linkage: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS as a production-telemetry-to-knowledge loop (H11) -- 'production-classified verify-completed events' are called out as a distinct, small subset (17 of 1,801) of the reported data, implying a production/non-production distinction exists in the underlying system, but the paper does not describe a mechanism by which production runtime observations specifically feed back into the shared knowledge/governance structure differently from synthetic or session events.
feedback_to_knowledge_mechanism: Present but explicitly immature: a 'Harness, measurement, and learning plane' (Table 4) and 'bounded learning feedback that stays off the hot path' (Fig.2 caption) are named in the architecture, and Table 17's capability-maturity snapshot rates 'Goal and progress monitor' as 'Scaffold' ('event types and partial specification exist, but no dedicated always-on monitor loop is reported') and 'Completion-admission check' as 'Live and advisory' -- the authors' own maturity table is unusually candid that this feedback loop is designed but only partially realized.
forward_traceability: Present via packet lineage and the append-only trace: 'a typical lineage is common-ground packet to claim packet to evidence packet to verify outcome' (Sec.6), and Fig.2 shows an 'append-only trace and governance log' fed by every branch outcome (accepted completion, blocked+recovery, failed/skipped, rollback) -- a structural design commitment, evidenced by the illustrative trace (Table 6) though not by a large-scale empirical trace-completeness measurement.
backward_traceability: Symmetric and explicit: 'restricted-audit event-taxonomy parity across active schema surfaces' and a 'monitored consistency scan reported 0 findings over 2255 tasks' (Table 16) are offered as structural-integrity evidence that the recorded packet/event trail can be checked against the schema after the fact -- a genuine, if narrowly-scoped (structural consistency, not full semantic reconstruction), H9 backward-traceability mechanism.
change_impact_mechanism: Partial: the recovery packet mechanism identifies 'who owns the next action' when a claim is blocked (Sec.3, Table 9: recovery packet requires 'next recovery action, recovery owner'), and rollback returns the system 'to a known safe state' (Table 7) -- a single-claim recovery-ownership assignment, not a multi-artifact dependency-propagation mechanism identifying other downstream decisions/requirements/artifacts affected by a changed or falsified upstream claim, so it falls short of D-System's H10 blast-radius claim.
human_agent_scope: Roles are described functionally rather than as distinctly human-only or AI-only (Table 5's nine roles carry no explicit human/AI typing); 'diagnostic-review-before-board' and a 'human-reviewed rollback policy' (Table 3) imply human involvement at high-risk escalation points, but the paper does not empirically evaluate human-AI collaboration (contrast this batch's omniscientist-coevolving-ecosystem-human-ai-scientists-2026, which does).
implementation_availability: Partial and explicitly bounded: 'No public repository for the internal reference implementation accompanies this manuscript... not the internal orchestration code, private prompts, or the private operating environment' (Code availability statement) -- only Supplementary Information (a tabulated synthetic event sample, ESM_1.pdf) and a 'supplementary accounting and schema package' (schema definitions, pseudocode, documentation notes) are released; the underlying system is an internal, unreleased reference implementation.
evaluation_method: An unusually self-critical bounded case-study snapshot, not a benchmark: event-level verify-outcome accounting (1,801 rows, Table 16), a shadow PGV advisory evaluation (n=2044, 98.58% rule agreement, 0% false-success, 0.39% blocked precision), structural-integrity checks (event-taxonomy parity, config lint, consistency scan over 2255 tasks), and an ancillary second-project portability check on an anonymized Rust workspace (Sec.11.1) -- the paper's own Table 1 and Discussion explicitly enumerate what is and is not claimed (no task-level success rate, no gated-vs-ungated ablation, no production-reliability claim, no multi-project generalization).
strongest_dsystem_overlap: The five-plane architecture's task-state tuple, formally specified fail-closed acceptance predicate gating every completion claim, packet-lineage provenance chain (common-ground -> claim -> evidence -> verify outcome), three-class memory-ownership taxonomy (canonical/archive-only/prompt-injectable) with an explicit context compiler shaping role-specific context envelopes, and risk-tiered (Light/Standard/Deep) execution-unit boundaries together constitute one of this campaign's closest structural matches to D-System's combined H2, H5, H8 and H9 claims -- notably, its context compiler distinguishing canonical/archive-only/prompt-injectable memory is a more developed, explicitly-named version of exactly the context-selection discipline D-System's H5 proposes but, per the adversarial codebase review, does not yet fully implement.
strongest_difference: No ontological/epistemic state classification (H1 absent -- the task-state tuple's dimensions are governance/operational, not an O,E,L triple); no independence-aware convergence mechanism (H4 absent -- PGV is a redundant advisory check on the same claim, not corroboration across independent paths); no requirement/specification-derivation chain from upstream reasoning or evidence (H7's early stages absent -- success criteria are asserted at task-ingest, not derived); no multi-artifact change-impact/blast-radius propagation (H10 only partially present, scoped to single-claim recovery ownership); the paper is unusually explicit about its own evidentiary limits -- the released empirical slice is 'synthetic-heavy and concentrated' (1,784/1,801 non-production rows, 1,762/1,801 from one reporting cluster), so quantitative claims validate inspectability, not effectiveness.

citation: Roper, W. Jr., Benson, C.L., Krishnan, S., Galvin, P., Abunojaim, B.E.A., Doijode, P.S., Abu Rmaileh, N.A. (Istari Digital, Inc.): Software-Code-Defined Digital Threads in Digital Engineering Systems with Artificial Intelligence (AI) Assistance. US Patent Application US20250165226A1, published 2025-05-22 (filed 2024-03-10, priority 2023-03-10, application no. US18/730,782). NOTE: confirmed via the patent's own legal-status metadata to have since GRANTED as US12461717B2 (status='Granted', grant number confirmed directly in the page's raw HTML, not merely from a WebFetch summary).
problem_addressed: How to reduce the largest cost driver in digital engineering -- manual, ongoing integration of siloed engineering-model tools (CAD, simulation, etc.) by specialized engineers -- by training a machine-learning model to automatically generate a 'platform orchestration script' (a 'software-code-defined digital thread') that connects two engineering models' representations to satisfy a stated intent, and storing/refining that script through user feedback.
state_model: NOT_APPLICABLE as an O,E,L classified state -- core objects are informally typed: 'model representation' (a structured export of an engineering model), 'intent input' (a natural-language or structured goal statement), and the generated 'platform orchestration script' (the digital thread itself); claim 1 ties these together but assigns no ontological/epistemic/lifecycle classification to any of them.
transition_model: The claimed mechanism (claim 1) is a single generative transition: a script-generating ML model, trained on (intent, model-representation-set, orchestration-script) triplets, maps a new (intent, first model representation, second model representation) input to a generated orchestration script -- a real intent-to-artifact transition, untyped beyond this one generation step; claim 2 adds a feedback-driven retraining transition ('receive a feedback data on the platform orchestration script... train and/or fine-tune the... model based on the feedback data'), the closest analogue to a typed knowledge-update transition.
provenance_model: Training-data provenance is explicit but narrow: each training triplet records which intent input, model-representation set, and orchestration script were used together (claim 1), and claim 3 has the system 'record[] the engineering models, model representations, intent input, endpoints, and user-defined orchestration script to generate training datasets' -- real data-lineage for retraining, but no actor-identity, domain-authority, or reliability field is claimed; provenance here means training-example lineage, not epistemic actor-attributed provenance.
actor_model: A single 'user' role selects engineering models and may write orchestration-script code directly (claim 3: 'receive a plurality of user selections... receive a user-defined code for a user-defined platform orchestration script') -- no multi-actor, human-vs-AI, or authority-weighted model; the ML model itself is not represented as an actor with identity.
temporal_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no valid-time/transaction-time or versioned-history model in the claims; the specification (outside the claims) mentions digital threads 'linked across different stages... of a product life cycle,' implying a lifecycle-ordered sequence, but this is descriptive background context, not a claimed temporal-query mechanism.
conflict_trust_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no claimed mechanism for arbitrating between competing scripts, models, or claims.
convergence_independence_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed.
memory_model: The training dataset of (intent, model-representations, script) triplets functions as the system's persistent memory of past successful connections, continuously extended by claim 3's data-recording mechanism and claim 2's feedback loop -- a genuine, if narrow, accumulating memory of prior intent-to-script mappings used to improve future generation, rather than a general knowledge/experience memory.
retrieval_context_model: NOT_APPLICABLE as a topology-aware context-selection mechanism -- the claimed process receives exactly two model representations and one intent input per generation call (claim 1); no described mechanism for selecting which prior threads, evidence, or context to retrieve/assemble beyond the training corpus used to fit the ML model.
decision_representation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no explicit decision object; the 'intent input' is the closest analogue to a directive, but is not represented with alternatives considered or rationale.
requirement_derivation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no requirement concept; the intent input functions as an ad hoc, per-call natural-language or structured goal statement, not a typed requirement derived through a chain from upstream evidence or decisions.
specification_representation: NOT_APPLICABLE in D-System's structured sense -- the 'model representation' (a structured export/description of an engineering model, e.g. CAD or simulation) is a specification of the engineering artifact being connected, not of the software system's own requirements or design; the generated orchestration script itself functions as an executable specification of how two models are to be connected.
planning_model: NOT_APPLICABLE within the claims read -- the specification's 'DE task DAG' (a Directed Acyclic Graph of scripted, pipelined engineering tasks, discussed with reference to an unexamined FIG. 10) is the closest analogue to a multi-step plan, but this DAG concept appears in background/preferred-embodiment material rather than in claims 1, 2, 3 or 25 as read.
execution_unit_session_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no phase/session boundary is claimed; each orchestration-script generation call (claim 1) is a single, stateless request-response unit with no persistent session identifier.
artifact_code_linkage: The patent's central and most concretely claimed mechanism: the generated 'platform orchestration script' is itself the code artifact, explicitly 'stored... as the software-code-defined digital thread' (claim 1) and directly linking two named engineering-model artifacts -- a real, tightly-scoped instance of intent-to-code linkage, narrower than D-System's H7 idea-to-implementation chain (no requirement/specification/decision stages between intent and code) but a genuine mechanism match for the artifact-linkage primitive specifically.
test_verification_linkage: Present in the specification but outside the claims read: physical-prototype sensor data (accelerometers, temperature sensors) is described as being 'compared with the DTw's [digital twin's] simulations to confirm the product's performance and verify its design' -- a real design-verification-via-runtime-comparison mechanism, appearing in the digital-twin/physical-twin background material rather than in claims 1, 2, 3 or 25.
deployment_linkage: Present in the specification only: digital threads are described as being 'linked across different stages... from concept, design, testing, to production,' implying a production/deployment stage in the broader described system, though not recited in the claims read.
runtime_observation_linkage: Present in the specification only, and a genuine H11-adjacent mechanism: 'external sensory data' from 'physical sensors... on prototype' and 'physical environmental sensors' is 'collected, processed, and integrated' via API endpoints into the digital-twin representation and compared against simulation to verify design -- real production/prototype telemetry feeding into a comparison against the model, described in background/preferred-embodiment material rather than the specific claims examined (1, 2, 3, 25).
feedback_to_knowledge_mechanism: Claimed and concrete, though narrow: claim 2 ('receive a feedback data on the platform orchestration script; and train and/or fine-tune the script-generating ML model based on the feedback data') is a real, claimed closed loop from an outcome (feedback on a generated script) back into the generative model's own parameters -- model retraining, not revision of a separate symbolic knowledge structure.
forward_traceability: Present: the training triplet (intent, model-representation set, orchestration script) and the recorded call inputs (claim 3: engineering models, model representations, intent input, endpoints, orchestration script) together let a generated thread be traced forward from the intent that produced it to the resulting script artifact.
backward_traceability: Symmetric to forward: because each generation call's inputs and output are recorded as a training example (claim 3), a given orchestration script/digital thread can in principle be traced back to the specific intent input and model representations that produced it -- claimed at the level of one generation call, not a multi-stage reasoning chain.
change_impact_mechanism: Present, narrowly, in the claims themselves -- a correction to a prior NOT_APPLICABLE coding. Claim 18 claims to 'predict a change in one or more items of the second plurality of computer-aided-engineering models... based on a change in one of the items,' and claim 19 restates the same for the reverse direction between the two linked digital-thread model representations -- a real, narrow, pairwise claimed change-propagation primitive between two model artifacts. It does not propagate through decisions, requirements, plans, or tests from an epistemic-assumption change, so it remains a distant, not materially equivalent, analog to H10's blast-radius claim.
human_agent_scope: A single human 'user' interacts with an AI (ML) script-generation system; claim 3 explicitly supports a human-authored alternative path ('receive a user-defined code for a user-defined platform orchestration script') alongside the AI-generated path, so the system is explicitly human-and-AI-capable for producing the same artifact type, but no collaborative human-AI interaction protocol (negotiation, review, approval) is claimed, unlike this batch's omniscientist-coevolving-ecosystem-human-ai-scientists-2026 source.
implementation_availability: Commercial product: the assignee, Istari Digital, Inc., operates the 'Interconnected Digital Engineering Platform (IDEP)' the patent describes as a real, named commercial system, not merely a prosecution-only concept; the patent itself grants no license or code release, and this dispatch did not independently verify the shipped commercial product's current feature set against the patent's specific claims (patent claims describe the legally protected invention, not necessarily the full shipped product's behavior).
evaluation_method: NOT_APPLICABLE -- patents do not require or report empirical evaluation; no benchmark, ablation, or comparative study is part of the document.

citation: Rasmussen, P., Paliychuk, P., Beauvais, T., Ryan, J., Chalef, D. (Zep AI): Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory. arXiv preprint, v1 20 Jan 2025.
problem_addressed: LLM agents need dynamic, continuously-evolving memory drawn from ongoing conversations and business data, not the static-corpus document retrieval traditional RAG provides; Zep addresses this via Graphiti, a temporally-aware knowledge graph engine that ingests and synthesizes unstructured conversational data and structured business data non-lossily while maintaining historical relationships.
state_model: Three-tier hierarchical graph G=(N,E,phi): Episode subgraph (raw, non-lossy input: messages/text/JSON), Semantic Entity subgraph (extracted, resolved entities and facts), and Community subgraph (label-propagation clusters with LLM-generated summaries) -- explicitly motivated by 'psychological models of human memory... episodic memory, which represents distinct events, and semantic memory, which captures associations between concepts' (Sec.2, ref.[8]) -- a two-type (episodic/semantic) distinction structurally adjacent to, but narrower than, D-System's three-axis (O,E,L) classification: no explicit epistemic-confidence or lifecycle-stage field per node, only structural subgraph membership.
transition_model: A genuine, formally described typed-transition mechanism: new fact edges are compared by an LLM against semantically related existing edges to detect contradictions, and 'when the system identifies temporally overlapping contradictions, it invalidates the affected edges by setting their t_invalid to the t_valid of the invalidating edge' (Sec.2.2.3) -- an explicit assert-invalidates-prior-fact transition rule, closely paralleling this campaign's tgms-agent-native-bitemporal-graph-2026 source's assert/retract/correct primitives, though Zep's transition carries no actor/method/evidence provenance field, only the four bitemporal timestamps themselves.
provenance_model: Minimal: episodic edges maintain 'bidirectional indices that track the relationships between edges and their source episodes... enabling both forward and backward traversal: semantic artifacts can be traced to their sources for citation or quotation' (Sec.2.1) -- a real source-lineage link from a derived fact back to the raw message/episode that produced it, but the paper explicitly notes 'these connections are not directly examined in this paper's experiments'; no actor-identity, authority, or method field beyond the episode-to-fact link itself.
actor_model: Minimal: 'the speaker is automatically extracted as an entity' from each message during entity extraction (Sec.2.2.1) -- the message's author becomes a graph entity, a basic actor-attribution link between an utterance and its speaker, but no authority/reliability weighting, and no distinction between human and AI-agent speakers is modeled.
temporal_model: The paper's central, most rigorously specified contribution and a direct H2/temporal-model match: 'Zep implements a bi-temporal model, where timeline T represents the chronological ordering of events, and timeline T' represents the transactional order of Zep's data ingestion' (Sec.2.1); four timestamps (t_created, t_expired in T'; t_valid, t_invalid in T) are stored per edge (Sec.2.2.3), and the paper states this 'bi-temporal approach represents a novel advancement in LLM-based knowledge graph construction' -- though the underlying valid-time/transaction-time distinction itself is the classical bitemporal-database model (see derivative_ancestor), and this paper's own reference list does not cite that lineage, framing the technique as novel relative to prior LLM/RAG memory systems specifically, not relative to temporal-database theory generally.
conflict_trust_mechanism: Present, narrow, and rule-based rather than weighted: contradiction detection uses a single mechanism (LLM comparison of a new edge against semantically related existing edges) and resolution is deterministic and recency-biased -- 'Following the transactional timeline T', Graphiti consistently prioritizes new information when determining edge invalidation' (Sec.2.2.3) -- no independence-, authority-, or evidence-weighted arbitration; the newer transactional entry always wins.
convergence_independence_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed; no mechanism discounts or weights agreement between multiple independent sources reporting the same fact.
memory_model: The paper's central subject and a direct, explicit H5/memory-architecture match: dual episodic (raw, non-lossy) and semantic (extracted, resolved) storage explicitly modeled on psychological dual-memory theory (Sec.2, ref.[8]), with a third community-summary tier built on GraphRAG's approach (ref.[4]) providing 'a more comprehensive, interconnected view' at the highest level of abstraction -- a materially close structural analogue to D-System's proposed memory model, scoped to conversational/business-data agent memory rather than general knowledge-and-development provenance.
retrieval_context_model: The paper's other central contribution and a direct H5 match: memory retrieval is formalized as f(alpha) = chi(rho(phi(alpha))), a three-stage Search-Rerank-Constructor pipeline (Sec.3) where Search combines cosine similarity, BM25 full-text, and graph breadth-first search ('phi_bfs... enhances initial search results by identifying additional nodes and edges within n-hops... allowing the system to incorporate recently mentioned entities and relationships into the retrieved context'), Rerank applies RRF/MMR/graph-distance/cross-encoder methods, and Constructor formats the final text-string context -- a genuine, formally specified, topology-aware (BFS-based) context-assembly mechanism, though it selects by semantic/lexical/graph-proximity relevance rather than by reasoning-lineage, dissent, or independence-weighted convergence as D-System's H5 proposes.
decision_representation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no decision object; Zep represents facts and entities, not choices or their rationale.
requirement_derivation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no requirement concept.
specification_representation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no specification concept.
planning_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no development-plan concept.
execution_unit_session_model: Partial: episodes are ingested per-message with reference timestamps within a conversational 'session' structure implied by the DMR/LongMemEval benchmark framing (multi-session conversations), but Zep itself does not define an explicit, bounded session/phase object with acceptance criteria -- sessions are an artifact of the evaluation datasets used, not a first-class Zep construct described in the architecture sections.
artifact_code_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no source-code or build-artifact concept; ingested data is conversational messages, text, or JSON business data, not software artifacts.
test_verification_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE as D-System's requirement-satisfaction test linkage -- the paper's own evaluations (DMR, LongMemEval) test Zep's retrieval accuracy against benchmark question/answer pairs, a system-evaluation activity, not a modeled verification-linkage primitive within the knowledge graph itself.
deployment_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no deployment concept within the graph model; Zep is itself a deployed commercial service (getzep.com) but the paper does not model 'deployment' as a graph entity/stage.
runtime_observation_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE as D-System's H11 production-telemetry-to-knowledge loop -- Zep's episodes ARE runtime data (live conversation/business-data ingestion) continuously updating the graph, structurally adjacent to a runtime-to-knowledge loop, but the paper frames this as ordinary operation (memory ingestion) rather than a distinct telemetry/incident-driven knowledge-revision mechanism separate from normal fact updates.
feedback_to_knowledge_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE as a distinct mechanism -- ordinary edge invalidation (Sec.2.2.3) is the paper's only knowledge-update pathway; there is no separate outcome/feedback signal (e.g., a retrieval marked wrong) that revises the graph differently from a new conversational fact would.
forward_traceability: Present and explicitly named, though unexamined empirically: 'episodic edges... maintain bidirectional indices that track the relationships between edges and their source episodes. This design reinforces the non-lossy nature of Graphiti's episodic subgraph by enabling both forward and backward traversal... episodes can quickly retrieve their relevant entities and facts' (Sec.2.1) -- the authors state 'these connections are not directly examined in this paper's experiments... they will be explored in future work.'
backward_traceability: Symmetric to forward and the same explicitly-named mechanism: 'semantic artifacts can be traced to their sources for citation or quotation' via the same bidirectional episode-to-entity indices (Sec.2.1) -- a genuine, if experimentally unvalidated in this paper, H9 backward-traceability primitive from a derived fact back to its originating message.
change_impact_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- edge invalidation (Sec.2.2.3) updates the specific contradicted edge only; no mechanism propagates a fact change to identify other dependent facts, entities, or community summaries that should be reassessed (community summaries are refreshed only periodically/heuristically via the label-propagation dynamic extension, Sec.2.3, not change-triggered).
human_agent_scope: The system serves LLM agents' memory needs with human users as message authors/speakers extracted as graph entities (Sec.2.2.1), but the paper models no collaborative human-AI interaction protocol, review/approval step, or distinct human-vs-agent authority -- humans are a data source (message speakers), not a distinguished participant class.
implementation_availability: Real, production, commercially deployed system: Zep is 'a commercial memory layer for AI applications' (ref.[5], getzep.com) built on Graphiti, an open-source component (ref.[6], github.com/getzep/graphiti); the paper states 'the experimental notebooks will be made publicly available through our GitHub repository.'
evaluation_method: Two established third-party benchmarks, not the authors' own construction: Deep Memory Retrieval (DMR, 500 multi-session conversations, from the MemGPT paper) where Zep achieves 94.8% (gpt-4-turbo) and 98.2% (gpt-4o-mini) versus MemGPT's reported 93.4%; and LongMemEval_s (~115,000-token conversations, six question types) where Zep improves accuracy by up to 18.5% and reduces latency by approximately 90% (2.58s vs 28.9s at gpt-4o) versus a full-context baseline -- the paper itself flags DMR as a weak benchmark ('the dataset poorly represents real-world enterprise use cases') and reports one own-result regression (single-session-assistant questions decreased 9.06-17.7% versus full-context).
strongest_dsystem_overlap: Graphiti's bi-temporal edge model (four timestamps: t_created/t_expired on the transactional timeline T', t_valid/t_invalid on the world timeline T) with LLM-mediated contradiction detection and recency-prioritized edge invalidation is a direct, load-bearing match to D-System's H2 typed-transition claim; its three-stage Search-Rerank-Constructor retrieval pipeline (including breadth-first graph traversal to incorporate 'recently mentioned entities and relationships') is a direct, formally specified match to D-System's H5 topology-aware context-transfer claim; and its explicitly-named (if experimentally unexamined) bidirectional episode-to-fact indices are a direct H9 backward/forward-traceability primitive.
strongest_difference: No ontological/epistemic classification beyond the episodic/semantic/community subgraph-membership distinction (H1 only partially present); no actor-authority or evidence-based provenance weighting -- edge invalidation is purely recency-based ('Graphiti consistently prioritizes new information'), not evidence- or authority-weighted (H3 largely absent); no independence-aware convergence mechanism (H4 absent); no requirement/specification/decision/artifact/verification/deployment concept anywhere -- the system is scoped entirely to D-System's Knowledge-Construction side, with no analogue of D-System's Implementation & Experience system at all (H7's software-development stages, H8's phase-bounded execution units, and H11's production-runtime loop are NOT_APPLICABLE by domain, not falsified); and its bi-temporal model, while presented as 'a novel advancement... in LLM-based knowledge graph construction,' inherits (without citing) the classical valid-time/transaction-time database-theory distinction this campaign's tgms-agent-native-bitemporal-graph-2026 source names explicitly.
derivative_ancestor: This dispatch's own tgms-agent-native-bitemporal-graph-2026 matrix row (read earlier in this campaign) explicitly names Zep as a sibling sharing one classical ancestor rather than an independent invention: TGMS Sec.7 states 'TGMS shares the bi-temporal foundation of Zep and TOKI but targets temporal graph analytics' and names Snodgrass, R.T.: Developing Time-Oriented Database Applications in SQL, Morgan Kaufmann, 1999, as the classical source of the valid-time/transaction-time distinction all three systems' bi-temporal substrates rest on. This Zep paper's own reference list (28 entries, read in full) does NOT cite Snodgrass or any classical temporal-database-theory work -- it presents its bi-temporal model as a novel advancement 'in LLM-based knowledge graph construction' specifically (defensible relative to prior LLM/RAG memory systems) while silently inheriting the underlying valid-time/transaction-time concept from that older, uncredited database-theory lineage. Recorded per this dispatch's coordinator instruction: one shared 1999 ancestor plus two derivative LLM-era applications (Zep and TGMS), not two independent corroborations of bi-temporal novelty. Separately, the paper's own dual episodic/semantic memory design is explicitly attributed (Sec.2) to Wong Gonzalez, D.: PhD thesis, University of Winsor, 2018 (ref.[8]) and to a contemporaneous sibling, AriGraph (Anokhin et al., 2024, ref.[9]); its community-subgraph/summarization approach explicitly builds on GraphRAG (Edge et al., 2024, ref.[4]).
evidence_locator: Abstract (p.1); Sec.2 Knowledge Graph Construction, graph formalism G=(N,E,phi) (p.2); Sec.2.1 Episodes, bidirectional episode-to-entity indices (pp.2-3); Sec.2.2.1-2.2.3 Entities, Facts, Temporal Extraction and Edge Invalidation, bi-temporal model and four timestamps (p.3); Sec.2.3 Communities, label-propagation dynamic extension (p.4); Sec.3-3.2 Memory Retrieval, Search/Reranker/Constructor formalism (pp.4-5); Sec.4.2-4.3 DMR and LongMemEval results, Tables 1-3 (pp.6-7); Sec.5 Conclusion (p.8); References [1]-[28] (pp.10-12).

citation: Lebo, T., Sahoo, S., McGuinness, D. (eds.): PROV-O: The PROV Ontology. W3C Recommendation, 30 April 2013.
problem_addressed: Define a vendor/domain-agnostic OWL2 vocabulary for interchanging provenance information (what entity was generated/used/derived by what activity, attributed/associated with what agent, including delegation) across independently-built Semantic Web systems.
state_model: No general ontological/epistemic/lifecycle state model; prov:Entity carries no built-in typed classification beyond informal wasRevisionOf/specializationOf relations for entity versioning. NOT_DETERMINABLE as an epistemic axis -- the ontology has no belief/claim-status vocabulary at all. Covers roughly the 'O' (ontological identity) slice of D-System's candidate S=(O,E,L,...), nothing of E or L.
transition_model: Activities connect entities via generation/usage/derivation edges (Entity --wasGeneratedBy--> Activity --used--> Entity), structurally close to D-System's S_t--[T,P]-->S_t+1 primitive, but PROV-O supplies no closed vocabulary of transition TYPES (no VALIDATE/FALSIFY/DECIDE-style taxonomy) -- applications must subclass/subproperty their own (as evidence-graphs-fair-computation-defeasible-reasoning-2021's EVI does when declaring directlySupports a PROV subproperty). PROV-O is a substrate, not a typed-transition taxonomy.
provenance_model: This IS the provenance model: Entity/Activity/Agent plus wasGeneratedBy/used/wasDerivedFrom/wasAttributedTo/wasAssociatedWith/actedOnBehalfOf/wasInformedBy, with qualified forms (Derivation, Usage, Generation, Attribution) for detailed provenance and Activity-level startedAtTime/endedAtTime. The standards-track ancestor whose shape D-System's own 'transition provenance' vocabulary (actor identity, method, lineage) directly echoes.
actor_model: prov:Agent with three built-in peer subclasses (Person, SoftwareAgent, Organization) plus actedOnBehalfOf for delegation chains; wasAssociatedWith links an Activity to a responsible Agent, optionally qualified with a Role. No authority/reliability/domain-expertise weighting is defined -- delegation depth is representable but not scored.
temporal_model: Activity-scoped instants only (startedAtTime/endedAtTime); no interval algebra, no valid-time/transaction-time (bitemporal) distinction, no as-of query semantics in the ontology itself (left to triple-store/query-engine implementations). NOT_APPLICABLE: no bitemporal model.
conflict_trust_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- the specification records what provenance is asserted, not whether it is true, contested, or more/less trustworthy; conflicting provenance assertions about the same entity can coexist in the graph with no built-in adjudication.
convergence_independence_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no notion of independent corroborating derivation paths strengthening confidence; left entirely to downstream applications, exactly as evidence-graphs-fair-computation-defeasible-reasoning-2021 must layer argumentation-theoretic support/challenge on top of PROV-O to get this at all.
memory_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- a provenance vocabulary, not an agent/LLM memory architecture; no retrieval, embedding, or episodic-boundary concept.
retrieval_context_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no purpose-built context-selection mechanism defined; PROV-O graphs are queried via generic RDF/SPARQL.
decision_representation: NOT_APPLICABLE in substance, though prov:Plan ('an entity that represents a set of actions or steps intended by one or more agents to achieve some goals') is defined and deliberately left abstract, 'to be extended by applications.' No rationale/alternatives/criteria structure.
requirement_derivation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- out of scope for a provenance ontology.
specification_representation: NOT_APPLICABLE.
planning_model: NOT_APPLICABLE beyond the abstract prov:Plan entity noted above, which is not an executable or structured planning representation.
execution_unit_session_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- prov:Activity is a generic 'occurs over a period of time' primitive, not a session/phase/task-boundary construct; an application could subclass Activity for this, but PROV-O itself defines no such unit.
artifact_code_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE in the ontology itself -- entities are untyped beyond 'physical, digital, conceptual, or other kind of thing'; an application must subclass Entity to represent source code or build artifacts, exactly as procko-provtracer-erau-dissertation-2025 and us20250165226a1-ai-digital-thread-patent do downstream.
test_verification_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE.
deployment_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE.
runtime_observation_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE.
feedback_to_knowledge_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- PROV-O records history; no defined mechanism by which recorded provenance revises upstream knowledge or belief.
forward_traceability: Structurally supported via wasGeneratedBy/used chains walkable forward through a provenance graph, but this is generic RDF-graph traversal capability the ontology's edges enable, not a purpose-built forward-traceability query language of its own.
backward_traceability: Symmetric to forward_traceability: wasDerivedFrom and the inverse of used/wasGeneratedBy support walking a derivation chain backward to its ultimate sources -- the data-lineage/digital-thread use case multiple descendant sources in this batch (procko-provtracer-erau-dissertation-2025, lineagerag-2026, evidence-graphs-fair-computation-defeasible-reasoning-2021) build directly on.
change_impact_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- prov:wasInvalidatedBy exists as a predicate (an Entity ceases to exist / becomes inapplicable at a point in time) but no downstream-impact propagation to dependent entities is specified.
human_agent_scope: Agent-type-agnostic by design: Person, SoftwareAgent and Organization are peer subclasses of the same Agent class with identical relation vocabulary, so human and automated actors are represented uniformly; no distinct human-vs-AI-agent semantics (unsurprising, predating LLM agents by roughly a decade).
implementation_availability: Foundational and near-universally implemented: reference toolkits (ProvToolbox, the prov Python library), adoption across dozens of independent provenance-tracking systems, and confirmed as the direct substrate this dispatch's own procko-provtracer-erau-dissertation-2025 and evidence-graphs-fair-computation-defeasible-reasoning-2021 rows build on.
evaluation_method: NOT_APPLICABLE -- a standards document; validated through the W3C Working Group process (implementation reports, interoperability testing across multiple independent OWL implementations), not an empirical study.
strongest_dsystem_overlap: The single closest raw-vocabulary antecedent to D-System's 'transition provenance' primitive (H2, H3, H7, H9): Entity/Activity/Agent plus generation/usage/derivation/attribution/association/delegation is structurally the same shape as D-System's candidate provenance record (actor identity, method, lineage, delegation) minus the epistemic/lifecycle axes and minus any typed-transition taxonomy, conflict arbitration, or convergence/independence weighting -- exactly the layer D-System's hypotheses claim as distinguishing additions on top of a substrate like this one.
strongest_difference: PROV-O is deliberately silent on everything H1-H11 claim as novel: no epistemic/lifecycle classification, no typed-transition taxonomy beyond generic generation/usage/derivation, no conflict/trust arbitration, no independence-aware convergence, no requirement/specification/plan/execution/test/deployment/runtime linkage, and no feedback-to-knowledge loop. It is the substrate three other rows in this campaign (procko, evidence-graphs, omniscientist) independently build that missing machinery on top of.
derivative_ancestor: Two named ancestors per the W3C Provenance Working Group's own documentary history (PROV-Overview, https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-overview/): (1) the Open Provenance Model (OPM), the community consensus model from the 2006-2010 'Provenance Challenge' series, whose lessons directly drove PROV's design; (2) PROV-DM, the sibling PROV specification defining the abstract conceptual data model PROV-O encodes in OWL2 -- PROV-O is an encoding, not an independent invention. Treat Provenance-Challenge/OPM -> PROV-DM -> PROV-O as one lineage, not three inventions, when assessing this dispatch's three PROV-O-descended rows.
evidence_locator: W3C TR https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/ Section 1 (Overview) for Entity/Activity/Agent class definitions and prov:Plan's abstract definition; Section 4 (Activities and Agents) for wasAssociatedWith/actedOnBehalfOf; Introduction for startedAtTime/endedAtTime; https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-overview/ and the W3C Provenance Working Group charter history for the OPM/Provenance-Challenge lineage.
verbatim_notes: 'prov:Entity ... a physical, digital, conceptual, or other kind of thing with some fixed aspects.' 'prov:Activity ... something that occurs over a period of time and acts upon or with entities.' 'prov:Agent ... something that bears some form of responsibility for an activity taking place.' prov:Plan is 'an entity that represents a set of actions or steps intended by one or more agents to achieve some goals' and is left 'to be extended by applications.' 'PROV-O is a lightweight ontology that can be adopted in a wide range of applications.'

citation: Perry, D.E. & Wolf, A.L.: Foundations for the Study of Software Architecture. ACM SIGSOFT Software Engineering Notes 17(4), Oct 1992, pp. 40-52.
problem_addressed: Establish a formal foundational model of what a 'software architecture' IS -- as a discipline distinct from requirements, design and implementation -- so architecture specifications can support consistency/dependency analysis and reuse.
state_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no typed knowledge-state model for individual items; the only 'state' concept is a whole architecture description (Elements/Form/Rationale), treated as a static specification artifact rather than a state machine of claims. NOT_DETERMINABLE as an analog to D-System's S=(O,E,L,...).
transition_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- the paper explicitly brackets process out of scope: 'we do not mean to imply anything about the particular process by which this product is created' (Sec 2.2). Architectural erosion/drift are named as motivating PROBLEMS of change over time, not modeled with any transition or versioning mechanism.
provenance_model: Rationale is 'an underlying, but integral, part of an architecture' that 'captures the motivation for the choice of architectural style, the choice of elements, and the form,' explicating 'the satisfaction of the system constraints' (Sec 3.1) -- prose-level, attached to the architecture as a whole, not a per-decision record with actor/timestamp/evidence fields.
actor_model: NOT_APPLICABLE structurally -- 'architect,' 'designer,' 'implementer,' 'user' are informal role-holders across the requirements/architecture/design/implementation layering (Sec 2.2); no formal Agent class, delegation relation, or authority/reliability model.
temporal_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no time representation; the paper is synchronic (a specification of one architecture), not a historical/temporal record.
conflict_trust_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no mechanism defined; 'competing architectures' (Sec 4.3, sequential vs. parallel compiler variants) appear only as an evaluation/comparison use case for consistency analysis, not conflict resolution or trust.

citation: Snodgrass, R.T.: Developing Time-Oriented Database Applications in SQL. Morgan Kaufmann, San Francisco, 1999. ISBN 1-55860-436-7.
problem_addressed: A comprehensive, implementer-facing treatment of how to design, query and modify time-varying data in a relational (SQL) database: formalizes the valid-time/transaction-time distinction and the resulting valid-time, transaction-time and bitemporal table structures, plus the SQL translation techniques (sequenced/nonsequenced/current modifications and queries) needed to support them without native temporal SQL support.
state_model: Defines two orthogonal temporal axes and their product: valid time ('when a fact was true in the modeled reality') and transaction time ('when a fact was stored in the database'), combining into bitemporal tables with four timestamp columns per row (Ch.10). A genuine state model, but purely temporal/positional -- no ontological or epistemic classification, NOT_DETERMINABLE as an analog to D-System's S=(O,E,L,...); 'state' here means 'the row(s) valid/recorded at a given instant,' not a typed knowledge-object classification.
transition_model: NOT_DETERMINABLE as a typed-transition taxonomy in D-System's sense -- defines nine categories of table MODIFICATION (insert/delete/update x current/sequenced/nonsequenced) as SQL translation patterns, not a closed vocabulary of semantically-typed transitions (no VALIDATE/FALSIFY/DECIDE-style types); modifications are mechanical operations on interval-stamped rows, not typed epistemic acts.
provenance_model: Transaction time IS effectively a minimal provenance/audit mechanism (when-recorded: 'the reconstructed state of a transaction-time table as of a point in the past will never change', p.250), but it records ONLY a timestamp -- never an actor, method, evidence, or reason. Confirmed absent throughout: no occurrence of 'provenance,' 'who asserted,' or comparable vocabulary anywhere in the full extracted text.
actor_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no notion of who recorded or asserted a fact; the book is agent-agnostic, addressing only WHEN a fact was true/recorded, never WHO recorded it or with what authority.
temporal_model: The book's entire subject and this dispatch's reason for reading it: formal valid-time/transaction-time/bitemporal semantics, interval-stamped rows, nine SQL modification categories, 'as-of' reconstruction queries (Ch.8-10), and the bitemporal time diagram (Ch.10) visualizing the four regions a fact's history can occupy. The single most rigorous temporal model read in this dispatch.
conflict_trust_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- confirmed absent (no 'conflict,' 'trust,' or source-authority vocabulary in the extracted text). Valid-time tables can be corrected/revised as new information arrives ('we are free to revise the stored history... as new information becomes available,' p.250), but there is no mechanism to represent or adjudicate two disagreeing valid-time assertions held simultaneously -- a later correction simply supersedes, it does not coexist as a competing claim.
convergence_independence_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no notion of independent corroborating sources; out of scope for a single-source-of-truth relational model.
memory_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- a database textbook predating agent/LLM memory concerns by roughly two decades; no retrieval or memory architecture, though the transaction-time append-only log is precisely the storage substrate zep-graphiti-temporal-kg-agent-memory-2025 and tgms-agent-native-bitemporal-graph-2026 repurpose for agent-memory use.
retrieval_context_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- retrieval is SQL query (as-of, sequenced, nonsequenced), not a context-selection mechanism for an agent.

D-System's H3 (provenance as conflict-resolution input) and H4 (independence-aware convergence) have no analog here -- this is the rawest possible substrate D-System's transition-provenance vocabulary would need to be built on top of, not a competing mechanism.

citation: Alchourron, C.E., Gardenfors, P., Makinson, D.: On the Logic of Theory Change: Partial Meet Contraction and Revision Functions. Journal of Symbolic Logic 50(2), 1985, pp. 510-530.
problem_addressed: Formalize, via minimal-rationality postulates, how a rational agent's set of beliefs (a logically-closed 'theory' K) should be minimally changed when contracting (removing) a belief or revising (incorporating a new, possibly contradicting) belief -- the founding formal theory of belief revision (the AGM postulates), defined axiomatically and via the partial-meet-contraction construction.
state_model: A single belief set K (K = Cn(K)) is the entire state representation -- a flat, untyped set of accepted sentences. NOT_APPLICABLE for ontological/epistemic/lifecycle multi-axis classification in D-System's S=(O,E,L,...) sense: AGM has exactly one epistemic status (member of K) plus, via epistemic entrenchment, a scalar ranking of how readily each belief would be given up -- not a typed classification (no claim/observation/evidence/inference/conclusion distinction).
transition_model: Two, and only two, transition operators defined axiomatically: contraction (K÷p) and revision (K*p), related by the Levi identity K*p = (K÷¬p)+p. A CLOSED, two-member typed-transition vocabulary -- narrower than D-System's open VALIDATE/FALSIFY/DECIDE-style taxonomy (H2), but the most formally axiomatized transition-type system in this batch; decision-oriented-programming-aporia-2026 and graph-native-cognitive-memory-belief-revision-semantics-2026 (both already in the matrix) build directly on exactly these two operators.
provenance_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- confirmed via secondary source (SEP) that AGM tracks no actor, timestamp, method or evidentiary source for why a sentence entered K; a belief's only recorded property beyond membership is its epistemic-entrenchment rank, a purely formal, source-agnostic minimal-change criterion.
actor_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- AGM models a single reasoner's belief set; per SEP: 'The beliefs held by an agent are represented by a set of...sentences,' with no second agent, delegation, or authority. Multi-agent merge operations are noted by SEP as extensions beyond core AGM, not part of the 1985 paper.
temporal_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- purely a before/after (K vs. K÷p or K*p) transformation with no timestamps, intervals, or valid/transaction-time distinction; the postulates are atemporal logical constraints on a single transition, not a history.
conflict_trust_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE for trust/authority (no source-reliability concept exists), but genuinely central for LOGICAL conflict: revision (K*p) is specifically the operator for incorporating a belief that contradicts existing beliefs, resolved via epistemic entrenchment (least-entrenched conflicting beliefs given up first) -- a real, formal minimal-change conflict-resolution rule, keyed entirely to formal entrenchment ranking, never to actor authority, evidence quality, or corroboration.
convergence_independence_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- SEP confirms multi-source merge/fusion is explicitly an EXTENSION beyond the core 1985 AGM postulates, not addressed by this paper.
memory_model: NOT_APPLICABLE as an agent/LLM memory architecture -- a belief set is not a retrieval structure; this is nonetheless the formal foundation graph-native-cognitive-memory-belief-revision-semantics-2026 (already in the matrix) builds an LLM-agent memory system on top of.
retrieval_context_model: NOT_APPLICABLE.
decision_representation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no alternatives/criteria/rationale object; a 'decision' in AGM is which maximal non-implying subset(s) a selection function gamma picks (K÷p = intersect gamma(K perp p)), a purely formal choice function with no represented justification beyond the entrenchment ordering that induces it.
requirement_derivation: NOT_APPLICABLE.
specification_representation: The AGM postulates themselves ARE a rigorous formal specification (closure, success, inclusion, vacuity, extensionality, recovery for contraction; closure, success, inclusion, vacuity, consistency, extensionality for revision, plus supplementary postulates) -- an axiomatic constraint specification for what counts as a RATIONAL transition, not a specification of a system's own requirements or design.

feedback_to_knowledge_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE in D-System's runtime-evidence sense, though revision (K*p) IS itself the formal mechanism by which new information updates a belief set -- the closest formal analog in this batch to 'feedback revises knowledge,' but generic (any new sentence p), not scoped to runtime/test/deployment observations specifically.
forward_traceability: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no artifact/decision graph to traverse; a single transition (K to K÷p or K*p) is not a multi-stage lineage.
backward_traceability: NOT_APPLICABLE for the same reason -- AGM's postulates constrain a single before/after pair, not a queryable history of prior states; nothing to walk backward through (contrast Snodgrass 1999's as-of reconstruction, elsewhere in this batch, which IS a history).
change_impact_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE directly, though the partial-meet-contraction construction (selecting WHICH other beliefs must also be given up to remove p while preserving closure and consistency) is structurally a minimal-change-propagation computation -- the closest formal analog in this batch to change-impact analysis, but scoped to logical entailment within one flat belief set, not typed dependencies across a requirement/plan/artifact/test graph.
human_agent_scope: NOT_APPLICABLE / agent-agnostic in the human-vs-AI sense (1985, predates the distinction) -- 'agent' in AGM means an abstract rational reasoner, not specifically human or artificial; this scope-neutrality is precisely why graph-native-cognitive-memory-belief-revision-semantics-2026 could adopt it unmodified for an LLM-agent memory system four decades later.
implementation_availability: NOT_APPLICABLE as software from the paper itself -- a pure logic/mathematics paper; downstream implementations exist widely (e.g. this campaign's own epica OSS AGM runtime, already inventoried at D07) but are not part of this 1985 source.
evaluation_method: NOT_APPLICABLE -- a foundational theorem-and-proof paper (representation theorems relating partial meet contraction to entrenchment-based and other axiomatizations); no empirical evaluation, as expected of 1985 formal logic.
strongest_dsystem_overlap: The single most formally rigorous TYPED belief-transition system in this batch: two named, axiomatically-constrained operators (contraction, revision) over a closed belief set, with a genuine (if source-agnostic) minimal-change conflict-resolution rule via epistemic entrenchment -- structurally the closest precedent to D-System's H2 (typed transitions) and the conflict-resolution half of H3, and explicitly named as the formal ancestor of two other sources already in this matrix (decision-oriented-programming-aporia-2026, graph-native-cognitive-memory-belief-revision-semantics-2026) that apply these exact postulates to LLM-agent systems.
strongest_difference: Everything that makes D-System's provenance model 'provenance' (actor identity, domain authority, evidence, method, lineage, delegation) is entirely absent -- AGM's only recorded property of a belief is a scalar entrenchment rank, source-agnostic and history-free; a belief set has no memory of ITS OWN revision history (each transition is evaluated independently against the postulates, with no requirement that K÷p retain any trace of p or of why it was removed). D-System's H4 (independence-aware convergence) and H5 (topology-aware context transfer) have no analog: AGM's belief set is unstructured (no graph, no topology) and multi-source corroboration is explicitly named by secondary literature as a later EXTENSION beyond this 1985 core.

citation: Nii, H.P.: The Blackboard Model of Problem Solving and the Evolution of Blackboard Architectures (Part One). AI Magazine 7(2), 1986, pp. 38-53.
problem_addressed: Define precisely what 'the blackboard model of problem solving' is as a general architectural pattern (abstracted from the HEARSAY-II speech-understanding system, 1971-1976) for organizing knowledge and coordinating independent problem-solving modules through a shared data structure, and survey the diversity of blackboard-architecture implementations built on it.
state_model: The blackboard itself is the shared state: 'a global database' holding the 'problem-solving state data,' organized into 'one or more application-dependent hierarchies,' each level holding partial solutions in a distinct vocabulary. A genuine multi-level state organization, but the levels are DOMAIN/ABSTRACTION levels (e.g. phrases vs. words vs. phonemes in HEARSAY-II), not an ontological/epistemic/lifecycle triple; NOT_DETERMINABLE as a direct analog to D-System's S=(O,E,L,...).
transition_model: NOT_APPLICABLE as a typed-transition taxonomy -- knowledge sources 'produce changes to the blackboard,' but the paper does not name or type these changes (no VALIDATE/FALSIFY/DECIDE-style vocabulary); change is whatever a knowledge source's opaque internal procedure computes. 'There is no control flow; the knowledge sources are self-activating' (Fig.1 caption) -- coordination is reactive/event-driven, not typed-message-based.
provenance_model: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS -- the base model as read (pp.38-41) does not specify that a blackboard entry records which knowledge source wrote it, when, or why, but the paper's own abstract promises a 'detailed description of the model's components and their behavior' in the extended 'blackboard framework' section (pp.~42-46, not read in this pass); whether that section adds a provenance mechanism is undetermined from the pages inspected.
actor_model: Knowledge sources are 'logically independent' and 'self-activating' -- functionally equivalent peer agents, with no formal Agent class or authority/reliability weighting. Footnote 6 states explicitly: 'There is no control component specified in the blackboard model. The model merely specifies a general problem-solving behavior' -- the base model deliberately withholds any actor-authority or arbitration structure.
temporal_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no interval, timestamp, or valid/transaction-time concept in the pages read; the model describes an incremental, step-by-step solution-building PROCESS (one contribution at a time), not a temporal record of it.
conflict_trust_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE for content-level conflict/trust between disagreeing knowledge-source claims -- not addressed in the base-model definition. The closest analog, from the jigsaw-puzzle analogy (p.40): a 'monitor' who, when multiple people (knowledge sources) are simultaneously eligible to act, 'can choose one person from those with their hands raised' by some criterion (first-raised, bridges-two-solution-islands, etc.) -- competition for the RIGHT TO ACT, resolved by an ADDED control component the base model itself explicitly does not specify (footnote 6), not resolution of disagreeing content claims.
convergence_independence_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no notion of independent corroboration in the pages read; knowledge sources contribute complementary (not competing/corroborating) partial solutions to a single shared, non-redundant blackboard state.
memory_model: The blackboard itself -- a shared, hierarchically-organized, opportunistically-updated global data structure all reasoning components read from and write to -- is exactly the architectural pattern log-is-the-agent-event-sourced-reactive-graphs-2026 (already in this matrix) explicitly repurposes as an agent-memory substrate for coordinating multiple LLM-agent behaviors. decision_representation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no alternatives/criteria/decision object; a knowledge source's internal reasoning for producing a given blackboard change is opaque to the model.

implementation_availability: The paper itself is conceptual, but names numerous contemporaneous blackboard SYSTEMS built on the model (HEARSAY-II, HASP, and per the References list, work by Barbara Hayes-Roth on blackboard architecture, 1983/1985 tech reports) -- the model was extensively implemented by 1986, and its structural descendant in this campaign's own matrix (log-is-the-agent-event-sourced-reactive-graphs-2026) is a working OSS system.

strongest_dsystem_overlap: 'There is a global database called the blackboard, and there are logically independent sources of knowledge called the knowledge sources. The knowledge sources respond to changes on the blackboard. Note that there is no control flow; the knowledge sources are self-activating' (Fig.1 caption) -- this shared-mutable-state, reactive, no-direct-inter-component-calls coordination pattern is structurally close to D-System's own implemented architecture, where the frozen adversarial codebase review finds idea events, memory, and governance state independently read/written by different tools/agents with 'no generic node/edge identity model or one traversal API,' and is explicitly named by log-is-the-agent-event-sourced-reactive-graphs-2026 (already in this matrix) as its own direct architectural ancestor for exactly this reason.
strongest_difference: In the base-model pages read, the blackboard model has no epistemic classification, no typed-transition vocabulary, no provenance/actor-authority model, and no conflict-resolution mechanism for disagreeing content (only scheduling-level competition for the right to act, via an added, not-specified-by-the-base-model, control component per footnote 6). Every one of D-System's H2-H4 epistemic/provenance/conflict claims is a capability the base model explicitly leaves unspecified: 'There is no control component specified in the blackboard model. The model merely specifies a general problem-solving behavior' (footnote 6).
