citation: Burckhardt, S., Gillum, C., Justo, D., Kallas, K., McMahon, C., Meiklejohn, C.S.: Durable Functions: Semantics for Stateful Serverless. Proc. ACM Program. Lang. 5, OOPSLA, Article 133 (October 2021), 27 pages.
problem_addressed: How to give Functions-as-a-Service (serverless) applications reliable, persistent, replayable state and progress despite weak execution guarantees and compute-storage separation, without requiring the host language runtime to support checkpointing.
state_model: NOT_APPLICABLE as an O,E,L-classified epistemic state. DF's persisted state is purely operational: the 'history' is an append-only sequence of typed execution events (OrchestratorStarted, TaskScheduled, TaskCompleted, TimerFired, EventRaised, etc., Sec.6) per orchestration/entity instance, reconstructed by deterministic replay. No ontological, epistemic, or lifecycle classification is attached to any state -- it is a record of what happened, not what is believed or asserted.
transition_model: Structurally close to D-System's S_t--[T,P]-->S_t+1: each history entry is a typed event (a 'transition') that is deterministically replayed to reconstruct successor state, formalized via a replay-based operational semantics (Sec.6) proved bisimilar to a fault-free high-level model (Thm 6.4). But the 'P' component carries no epistemic provenance (no actor authority, evidence, or trust) -- only the data needed for deterministic replay (task id, result value).
provenance_model: NOT_APPLICABLE in the epistemic/actor-authority sense. The history log is provenance only in a narrow execution-correctness sense (which activity produced which result, in what order) -- there is no source-reliability, authority, or lineage-of-belief tracking.
actor_model: 'Entities' (Sec.3.3) are durable virtual actors in the Orleans tradition (Bykov et al. 2011, cited): they encapsulate state, process one operation at a time from a queue, and give exactly-once delivery guarantees for orchestration-to-entity messages. This is a compute/consistency actor model, not an epistemic-authority actor model -- entities have no notion of domain authority or trust weighting.
temporal_model: Implicit sequencing only: history entries are totally ordered per instance by the order they are recorded; 'eternal orchestrations' (Sec.3.2.3) use continue-as-new to bound unbounded history growth by periodically restarting with a fresh history. No explicit valid-time/transaction-time bitemporal model.
conflict_trust_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE. Determinism is enforced by construction (non-deterministic operations must be wrapped in activities, Sec.3.5) rather than resolved after the fact; there is no mechanism for reconciling conflicting claims or sources.
convergence_independence_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE. No notion of independent corroboration; a given orchestration has exactly one authoritative history.
memory_model: The per-instance history log IS the memory: durability is implicit (Sec.3.1) -- orchestration progress and entity state survive process failure purely by being reconstructable from the persisted, replayable history. This is the closest primitive to LangGraph's checkpoint mechanism (and to D-System's append-only state log), but scoped to one execution instance's operational state, not cross-session epistemic memory.
retrieval_context_model: NOT_APPLICABLE as a context-selection mechanism. Replay reconstructs local variables and control-flow position for the SAME instance; there is no retrieval across different instances/orchestrations and no notion of selecting relevant history for a downstream consumer.
decision_representation: NOT_APPLICABLE
requirement_derivation: NOT_APPLICABLE
specification_representation: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS beyond the formal operational semantics itself (the high-level lambda-calculus model, Sec.4, functions as a specification of correct DF behavior against which the two lower-level execution models are proved equivalent) -- this is a specification of the RUNTIME's behavior, not of a software requirement or design decision.
planning_model: NOT_APPLICABLE
execution_unit_session_model: Direct structural analog to D-System's phase/session concept: an 'orchestration instance' (identified by an explicit instance id, Sec.3.2.3) is the execution-unit boundary; continue-as-new explicitly re-bounds that unit when its history grows too large to replay efficiently (Sec.3.5) -- the same 'unbounded context growth' problem H8 raises for development phases, solved here for a serverless workflow's replay log rather than an agent's task context.
artifact_code_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE
test_verification_linkage: The paper's own verification is a formal proof (bisimulation between the compute-storage model and the replay-based model, Thm 6.4, Sec.6.3) that record-replay preserves the fault-free high-level semantics for deterministic orchestrations -- a correctness proof of the RUNTIME mechanism itself, not a test/verification-linkage mechanism for downstream software artifacts.
deployment_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE
runtime_observation_linkage: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS beyond the built-in status-query API (clients can query an orchestration instance's status by instanceId, Sec.3.2.3) -- this is operational monitoring of execution progress, not runtime evidence feeding back into a knowledge structure.
feedback_to_knowledge_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE
forward_traceability: NOT_APPLICABLE
backward_traceability: Strong within one execution instance: deterministic replay reconstructs the exact prior sequence of events an instance passed through (Sec.6), giving complete backward traceability of execution history -- but only for the operational/execution dimension, not idea-to-decision-to-code lineage.
change_impact_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE
human_agent_scope: Fully automated / machine-only. No human-in-the-loop epistemic content; humans appear only as the developers who author orchestrator code, not as participants whose beliefs or evidence enter the system's state.
implementation_availability: Yes -- Azure Durable Functions is a shipping, widely used production system (github.com/Azure/durabletask, cited in the paper's own references) with multiple storage backends (Azure Storage, MSSQL, Netherite); this OOPSLA paper is its formal semantics, not merely a design proposal.
evaluation_method: Formal: operational semantics + bisimulation proof (Sec.4-6) that the replay-based execution model is equivalent to a fault-free high-level model. No empirical performance evaluation in this paper (a companion Netherite backend paper, self-cited as arXiv:2103.00033, covers performance).
strongest_dsystem_overlap: The append-only, typed, replayable history log as the sole mechanism reconstructing an execution unit's state is a genuine structural collision with D-System's append-only transition log and with the checkpoint/replay pattern D-System's own architecture research (H8, phase-bounded context) and LangGraph's checkpointer draw on -- and this is a formally proven-correct instance of that pattern from a tradition (durable/stateful serverless) the campaign's domain sweep (D01-D72) did not include.
strongest_difference: The history/replay mechanism carries zero epistemic content -- no ontological/epistemic/lifecycle classification, no provenance in the belief/evidence/authority sense, no conflict or convergence handling, no linkage to requirements/decisions/artifacts/tests/deployment. It is a pure execution-correctness mechanism for one automated workflow instance, entirely orthogonal to D-System's knowledge-construction half (H1-H7, H9-H11) and only partially analogous to the session/context-boundary half (H8).
derivative_ancestor: Goldstein et al. 2020, A.M.B.R.O.S.I.A: Providing Performant Virtual Resiliency for Distributed Applications (VLDB, doi:10.14778/3377369.3377370) -- co-authored by the same lead author (Burckhardt) and cited in this paper's own references as the direct academic ancestor of the record-replay 'virtual resiliency' mechanism this paper specializes to the serverless/FaaS setting; also draws on Orleans virtual actors (Bykov et al. 2011, cited) for the entity/actor model. Not independent of that lineage.
evidence_locator: PDF (Microsoft Research open-access mirror, CC-BY 4.0, microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/DF-Semantics-Final.pdf): abstract; Sec.1 p.1-2 (problem statement); Sec.3.1 p.6 ('durability is implicit'); Sec.3.2.3 p.9-10 (eternal orchestrations, continue-as-new, instance id); Sec.3.3 p.10-11 (entities); Sec.3.5 p.12 (determinism requirement, history size); Sec.4-6 p.13-24 (formal models, Thm 6.4 bisimulation); References p.27 (A.M.B.R.O.S.I.A, Orleans citations).
verbatim_notes: "the internal state of a DF application, i.e., the state of all actors, queues, and the progress of all orchestrations, is not visibly affected by any transient faults or recoveries" (p.4, Sec.3.1). "Internally, DF persists and restores the intermediate state of an orchestration by recording and replaying task results in a history" (p.12, Sec.3.5) -- direct textual basis for the transition/memory-model comparison.

citation: Zimmermann, O., Koehler, J., Leymann, F., Polley, R., Schuster, N.: Managing Architectural Decision Models with Dependency Relations, Integrity Constraints, and Production Rules. Journal of Systems and Software 82(8), 1249-1267 (Aug 2009).
problem_addressed: How to formally model architectural decisions (and the reusable knowledge underlying them) as a graph of typed, dependency-linked entities so that dependency relations can be enforced by integrity constraints, decision-making can be guided by production rules, and the result can be verified for consistency -- moving decision capture from informal text templates to a checkable formal model.
state_model: ADOutcome instances carry an explicit lifecycle field: status in {open, implied, resolved} (Sec.3, Definition around outcome instances), plus finer distinctions (eligible/pending open outcomes based on triggers relations). This is a genuine lifecycle (L) classification on a decision-state primitive, though there is no separate ontological (O) or epistemic (E) axis -- status is purely decision-processing state, not a belief-type or evidence-type classification.
transition_model: The 'triggers' relation (Definition 11) is a formally defined causal transition: choosing alternative a_i triggers issue i_k, changing that issue's outcome status from not-yet-relevant to open/eligible/pending -- a typed, DAG-structured transition mechanism enforced by Integrity Constraints 5-8 (trigger compatibility, top-down progression). This is a materially close structural analog to D-System's S_t--[T,P]-->S_t+1 typed-transition semantics, scoped to architectural-decision state rather than general knowledge state.
provenance_model: ADOutcome instances carry a changedBy attribute (Sec.3, p.4-5, 'attributes that are required for lifecycle management ... of ADOutcomes in project-specific decision models (e.g., changedBy)') -- actor-identity provenance on each recorded decision outcome. No further provenance dimensions (evidence, method, delegation) are formalized beyond this attribute and free-text justification/rationale fields.
actor_model: Architects, project managers, and enterprise architects are named as distinct roles (role attribute on ADIssue, Sec.3; 'freedom of choice' vs 'freedom from choice' governance discussion, Sec.7) but the formal model itself (Sec.4-5) has no actor-authority or trust-weighting construct -- changedBy records who last modified an outcome, not a weighted authority.
temporal_model: NOT_APPLICABLE as a bitemporal or valid/transaction-time model in any formalized, elaborated sense. Sequencing is purely structural/causal (DAG topology via triggers, refinedBy, decomposesInto), not timestamped; Fig.1 (p.5) shows a validUntil: Timestamp attribute on ADOutcome, but it is never elaborated again in Sec.4-7 and no versioning or point-in-time query semantics are formalized around it, though the RADM for SOA case study (Sec.6.2) mentions the content 'was extended and refactored several times' since 2006 informally.
conflict_trust_mechanism: Formal logical-consistency mechanism, not a belief-trust mechanism: isIncompatibleWith / isCompatibleWith relations plus Integrity Constraints 3-4 mechanically forbid contradictory alternative combinations (an alternative that forces another cannot also be marked incompatible with it). This resolves logical conflicts among decision alternatives by construction, not epistemic conflicts among competing evidence or sources.
convergence_independence_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE. No notion of independent corroboration; each ADOutcome records exactly one resolved decision with one rationale, not multiple converging or dissenting claims.
memory_model: The Reusable Architectural Decision Model (RADM) itself, evaluated at 389 captured issues spanning >30 projects (Sec.6.2), functions as reusable organizational decision memory, separated into reusable background (ADIssue/ADAlternative) and project-specific outcome memory (ADOutcome) -- a two-tier memory model distinguishing generalizable knowledge from instance-specific application, structurally similar to D-System's distinction between durable knowledge state and situated transitions.
retrieval_context_model: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS beyond structural navigation: ADTopicGroup/ADLevel hierarchies and the scope attribute (linking an ADIssue to design-model element types, Sec.3) organize the model for browsing, and the Architectural Decision Knowledge Wiki tool (Sec.6, made public March 2008) presumably supports lookup, but no explicit context-selection or relevance-ranking algorithm is formalized in this paper.
decision_representation: The paper's central formal contribution: architectural decisions are DAGs of ADTopicGroup/ADIssue/ADAlternative/ADOutcome nodes connected by typed edges (containment/refinement, decomposesInto, triggers, forces, isIncompatibleWith, isCompatibleWith, dependsOn), governed by eight formally proved integrity constraints and production-rule-style dependency patterns (Sec.5, e.g. TECHNOLOGY LED DESIGN, VENDOR PUSH) -- one of the most formally complete decision-representation mechanisms found in this campaign, a direct H2/H7 match.
requirement_derivation: decisionDrivers (on ADIssue, types of non-functional requirements) and justification (on ADOutcome, 'refers to actual requirements', e.g. "sub-second response time in customer interface", Sec.3 p.4) formally separate reusable requirement TYPES from project-specific requirement INSTANCES bound to a decision outcome -- a concrete, if narrow, requirement-to-decision linkage.
specification_representation: NOT_APPLICABLE. The model stops at decision outcomes; no specification-language or executable-specification representation is defined for what an outcome, once resolved, specifies downstream.
planning_model: Envisioned but not implemented: Sec.7 (Conclusion) proposes that 'open issues correspond to required activities' so 'work breakdown structures and effort estimation reports can be created' from the decision model -- a plan-derivation idea stated as future/advanced usage, not a formalized or evaluated mechanism in this paper.
execution_unit_session_model: NOT_APPLICABLE. No notion of a bounded execution/session unit; the RADM is a persistent, continuously extended knowledge base (2006-2009 and beyond), not phase- or session-scoped.
artifact_code_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE. Decisions can reference 'design model element instances' by name via the scope mechanism (Sec.3), but no linkage to source code or build artifacts is defined.
test_verification_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE to software test/verification. The paper's own 'verification' is model-internal: integrity constraints (1-8) are checked against the decision model itself (a model is 'valid' or 'strictly valid' iff constraints hold, Sec.4) -- consistency checking of the decision graph, not of downstream code or requirements satisfaction.
deployment_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE
runtime_observation_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE
feedback_to_knowledge_mechanism: Partial: Sec.7 proposes 'health checking' -- if a project shows many frequent decision changes or many unresolved issues late in the project, the project is likely troubled -- but this is stated as a future usage scenario, not an implemented feedback loop from runtime/project outcomes back into the decision model.
forward_traceability: Present within the decision layer only: an ADIssue's reusable content forward-traces into project-specific ADOutcome instances (one issue -> many outcomes across processes/projects, Sec.3 example), and triggers relations forward-trace one decision into the issues it activates. Does not extend to requirements/spec/code/test/deployment.
backward_traceability: Symmetric to forward_traceability: an ADOutcome's justification and changedBy attribute allow tracing a specific decision back to its rationale and author, and triggers/forces relations can be traversed backward to find which alternative activated a given issue (used in the integrity-constraint proofs, Sec.4).
change_impact_mechanism: Constraint-propagation form of impact analysis: because forces/triggers/isIncompatibleWith relations and their integrity constraints (3, 6, 7) formally imply each other (e.g. IC6: a forces relation between alternatives implies a specific triggers relation), changing one relation can be checked for consistency against the rest of the DAG -- a structural, logic-based impact mechanism, not an epistemic blast-radius mechanism over evidence/assumptions (H10 is not matched; this is decision-graph consistency, not assumption-dependency propagation).
human_agent_scope: Fully human: architects, project managers, and enterprise architects author, harvest, and apply the decision model by hand (industrial action-research case study, Sec.6, collaborative wiki tool); no agentic/AI participant is present in this 2009 paper, though Sec.7's outlook speculates about a 'reasoning engine' over natural-controlled-language decision drivers as future work.
implementation_availability: Yes -- the Architectural Decision Knowledge Wiki (ADkwiki), 'made publicly available in March 2008' (Sec.6), is a working collaborative tool implementing the metamodel, plus the evaluated RADM for SOA content itself (389 issues).
evaluation_method: Three-part validation (Sec.6): (1) analytic comparison of the dependency-relation taxonomy against Kruchten et al.'s established taxonomy (Table 6, showing near-total conceptual coverage); (2) industrial content validation via the RADM for SOA case study (389 issues, >30 projects, stable since Sept 2006); (3) tool implementation (the public wiki). No controlled experiment or user study is reported.
strongest_dsystem_overlap: The most formally complete decision-representation and constraint-production-rule mechanism found in this campaign to date: an explicit outcome-status lifecycle field (open/implied/resolved), a formally proved typed-transition mechanism (triggers, governed by 8 integrity constraints), per-outcome actor provenance (changedBy), and a requirement-to-decision linkage (decisionDrivers/justification) together give strong, multi-primitive overlap with D-System's transition/provenance/decision-representation primitives (H2, H7) -- though confined to the decision/requirement stages, with no execution/artifact/test/deployment/runtime extension.
strongest_difference: The mechanism never leaves the decision-and-requirement layer: there is no specification, plan, execution, artifact, test, deployment, or runtime-evidence linkage (the work-breakdown-structure and health-checking ideas in Sec.7 are explicitly future work, not implemented mechanisms), no epistemic (belief-type) or ontological classification alongside the lifecycle status, no independence-aware convergence, and no blast-radius/change-impact mechanism over evidence or assumptions -- only over the decision graph's own logical consistency.
derivative_ancestor: Jansen, A. and Bosch, J.: Software Architecture as a Set of Architectural Design Decisions, WICSA 2005 (jansen-bosch-architecture-as-decisions-wicsa-2005, already in this matrix) -- the paper states explicitly (Sec.3, p.5) 'Our metamodel extends that from [1] and [5]' with [5] = Jansen and Bosch. This is a direct formal extension of an already-matrixed critical collision, not an independent confirmation; its own novel contribution is the integrity-constraint/production-rule formalization and the outcome-status/changedBy lifecycle fields, which go beyond Jansen and Bosch's original model. De Boer et al.'s QoSA 2007 paper [4] is explicitly noted (p.5) as 'developed independently of and simultaneously to our UML model' -- NOT an ancestor relationship, despite topical similarity to de-boer-architectural-knowledge-management-dissertation-2009 already in the matrix.
evidence_locator: PDF (author's camera-ready copy, soadecisions.org/download/SOAD-JSS82CameraReadyFinal.pdf, hosted by lead author Olaf Zimmermann; identity confirmed via DOI/Crossref against the published JSS 82(8):1249-1267 record, though this camera-ready PDF carries its own internal page numbering, 1-36, not the published journal pagination): Abstract p.1; Sec.3 p.3-6 (UML metamodel, status field, changedBy, decisionDrivers/justification); Sec.4 p.9-16 (triggers, forces, Integrity Constraints 1-8); Sec.5 p.20-29 (dependency patterns); Sec.6 p.29-31 (validation: taxonomy comparison, RADM for SOA content, ADkwiki tool); Sec.7 p.33-34 (Conclusion, envisioned WBS/health-checking future work); References p.34-36.
verbatim_notes: "we define attributes that are required for lifecycle management of ADIssues in the reusable part (e.g., role) and ADOutcomes in project-specific decision models (e.g., changedBy)" (PDF p.6, Rationale paragraph following Fig.1, Sec.3). "outcome instances O = {(name, candidateAlternatives, status) | name in Strings, candidateAlternatives subset A, status in {open, implied, resolved}}" (Definition 14, PDF p.22, Sec.4, outcome-status definition). "Our metamodel extends that from [1] and [5]" (PDF p.6, Sec.3) -- [5] is Jansen and Bosch, WICSA 2005, confirming the lineage recorded in derivative_ancestor.
second_review: disputed: flag and both scores independently reproduced and confirmed, but the row's own narrative overstates implementation maturity -- the triggers/integrity-constraint engine underlying the component score lives in a non-public prototype (Sec.6.3), separate from the widely deployed Architectural Decision Knowledge Wiki. The flag rests on a single trigger (component_overlap), not convergent evidence, contrary to the row's framing. Corrections applied: two quote-locator errors (a 6-page discrepancy on the outcome-status definition; a p.4-5-to-p.6 drift on two Sec.3 quotes), a false pagination-match claim removed from evidence_locator, and temporal_model amended to note the unelaborated validUntil attribute (Fig.1, p.5).

citation: Burns, G.A., Groth, P.: Complex Knowledge Curation using Agentic Ontological Notebook Memory. In: Proceedings of the 1st ACM Conference on AI and Agentic Systems (CAIS '26), May 26, 2026, San Jose, CA, USA. ACM, 5 pages.
problem_addressed: How to give LLM-agent memory explicit, testable, refinable domain-specific ontological commitments (entity types, typed relations, inference rules) instead of leaving semantic structure implicit in prompts/code or fully outsourced to LLM-extracted, corpus-shaped ontologies -- and how to provide provenance from an agent's generated analysis back to its concrete sources.
state_model: A genuine multi-part classification close to D-System's O/E/L triple: an ontological axis (domain things -- real-world entities like diseases, companies, systems -- vs Information Content Entities/ICEs, mirroring the W3C-adjacent Information Artifact Ontology's entity/representation split, Sec.3.3); an epistemic-adjacent derivational-depth axis within ICEs (Artifact = raw captured source, Fragment = structured extraction, Note = agent's own analysis/hypothesis, Sec.3.3); and, per-skill rather than universal, an explicit lifecycle axis (e.g. tech-recon's candidate->confirmed->ingested->analyzed pipeline, Sec.4.2, 'investigation progress is itself a queryable graph property'). Not a single universal O+E+L triple applied uniformly to every state (each skill defines its own schema extension), so distinct from but structurally close to H1.
transition_model: Weaker than D-System's typed S_t--[T,P]-->S_t+1: 'notes can be linked to notes' (Sec.3.3) gives an append-only, referenceable chain of agent analysis, and the per-skill status pipeline (candidate->confirmed->ingested->analyzed) is an implicit typed progression, but neither is formalized as a general typed-transition-with-provenance primitive the way Zimmermann et al.'s triggers relation or D-System's T is.
provenance_model: Direct, explicit match: 'Notes are always attributed to the agent and are linked to ICEs' (Sec.3.3) -- actor-identity provenance on every generated claim -- plus a full backward chain 'every note is linked to concrete information sources... the user can follow the chain back to the original database records' (Sec.3.3) and a live demo scenario explicitly 'inspecting the TypeDB graph to show provenance chains from notes through fragments to artifacts' (Sec.4.4). No source-authority/trust-weighting dimension beyond attribution.
actor_model: Single-actor provenance only (the agent itself, always the author of a Note); human users interact via natural language and maintain profiles (e.g. job-hunt skill's user-maintained skill profile) but are not modeled as authoritative sources with weighted trust distinct from the agent.
temporal_model: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS beyond implicit recency (knowledge graph 'grows in real time' as artifacts are ingested, Sec.4.4); no explicit valid-time/transaction-time bitemporal model is described, in contrast to Zep/Graphiti (cited in Sec.5 as maintaining historical relationships via a bi-temporal model) which this paper explicitly contrasts itself against.
conflict_trust_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE. No mechanism for reconciling conflicting notes or sources is described; TypeDB's role-based relationship typing (Sec.2) enforces structural/schema validity, not epistemic conflict resolution.
convergence_independence_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE. No notion of independent corroboration across notes or sources is described.
memory_model: The core contribution: a TypeDB-backed, schema-typed, persistent 'ontological notebook' per skill, structurally distinguishing raw content (Artifacts), extractions (Fragments), and agent analysis (Notes), explicitly contrasted (Sec.5, Related Work) against MemGPT/Letta's unstructured memory tiers, LangGraph's 'opaque key-value pairs rather than typed ontological structures', Zep/Graphiti's temporal KG, Mem0's three-backend approach, and Cognee's embedding+triplet extraction -- positioned as a genuinely distinct point in the same design space rather than an extension of any one of them.
retrieval_context_model: Dual-representation by design (Sec.5, 'Retrieval over knowledge graphs'): each entity is simultaneously a typed TypeDB node (for structural queries: counting, absence-detection, ranking) and an embedded text fragment (for semantic-similarity queries), routed to whichever is appropriate -- explicitly NOT a topology/dissent/authority-aware context-selection mechanism (H5 not matched); routing is by query TYPE (structural vs semantic), not by evidence lineage or unresolved uncertainty.
decision_representation: Present only in the tech-recon skill: 'success criteria' are 'promoted to first-class entities so that every note and analysis is anchored to an explicit evaluation dimension' (Sec.4.2) -- a narrow, domain-specific decision-criteria representation, not a general decision/outcome model like Zimmermann et al.'s.
requirement_derivation: NOT_APPLICABLE in a software-requirements sense; the closest analog is the job-hunt skill's extraction of 'structured requirements (technology stacks, experience levels, domain expertise)' from job postings (Sec.4.1) -- requirement extraction from an external document, not derivation of software requirements from knowledge/decisions.
specification_representation: NOT_APPLICABLE. Each skill's TypeDB schema extension is itself a specification of domain semantics, but not a specification of software behavior or requirements to be implemented.
planning_model: NOT_APPLICABLE beyond the informal candidate->confirmed->ingested->analyzed investigation pipeline (tech-recon skill), which sequences investigation activity but is not a general planning/task-decomposition mechanism.
execution_unit_session_model: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS as a bounded execution/session-context mechanism; the system supports 'Interactive Mode' (direct chat) and 'Agentic Mode' (an always-on scheduled service, Sec.3.1) but no explicit context-boundary or history-truncation mechanism analogous to H8 is described.

citation: Levinson, M.A., Niestroy, J., Al Manir, S., Fairchild, K., Lake, D.E., Moorman, J.R., Clark, T.: FAIRSCAPE: A Framework for FAIR and Reproducible Biomedical Analytics. Neuroinformatics 20(1), 187-202 (Jul 2021).
problem_addressed: How to build a reusable, cloud-based 'data commons' microservices framework that makes computational biomedical research fully FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) by automatically capturing machine-interpretable, persistently-identified provenance -- an Evidence Graph -- for every dataset, piece of software, and computation, so results can be validated, reproduced, and reused without requiring reviewers to actually re-run large-scale computations.
state_model: NOT_APPLICABLE as an O,E,L-classified knowledge state. FAIRSCAPE's core unit is a persistently-identified (ARK) object (dataset, software, computation, or evidence graph) with JSON-LD metadata; the EVI ontology it implements reuses W3C PROV's three classes (Entity, Activity, Agent) rather than an orthogonal ontological/epistemic/lifecycle classification -- the epistemic dimension (findings as 'defeasible components of argumentation' rather than facts) belongs to the EVI/evidence-graph mechanism this paper implements, not to a distinct contribution of this paper itself.
transition_model: Implicit rather than explicitly typed at the paper's own level: each Compute Service invocation takes PID-referenced inputs (dataset/script/container) and produces a PID-referenced output activity with 'provenance aware metadata' (Materials and Methods, Compute Service) -- structurally an Entity--[Activity]-->Entity transition in the PROV sense, inherited from the EVI ontology (Al Manir et al., already matrixed) rather than newly formalized here.
provenance_model: The paper's central operational contribution: every registered object and every computation automatically receives a complete, machine-resolvable Evidence Graph (a directed graph of PIDs for the datasets, software, and computations that produced it), built by a dedicated Evidence Graph microservice running a SPARQL PATH query over a Stardog graph store, with the graph's root URI embedded in the result's own metadata (Abstract; Evidence Graph Service). This operationalizes -- as a real running system -- the EVI/evidence-graph provenance model already captured in this matrix's evidence-graphs-fair-computation-defeasible-reasoning-2021 row.
actor_model: PROV's Agent class is reused (via EVI) for personnel/software agents involved in a computation (Abstract: 'personnel involved'); access control is handled separately by Keycloak/Globus Auth identity tokens (Authentication and Authorization Layer) -- an access-control actor model, not an epistemic-authority or trust-weighting one.
temporal_model: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS beyond object versioning (the Object Service supports 'uploading new versions of existing files', Materials and Methods) and job-completion timestamps implicit in PID metadata; no explicit bitemporal (valid-time/transaction-time) model is described.
conflict_trust_mechanism: Inherited from EVI, not newly defined here: the paper states the framework is designed to support 'propagation of evidence challenges deep in the graph, such as: retractions, reagent contamination, errors detected in algorithms, disputed validity of methods' (Introduction), but this paper does not itself define the challenge/defeat semantics -- that is the EVI ontology's contribution (the already-matrixed evidence-graphs source), which FAIRSCAPE operationalizes as infrastructure.
convergence_independence_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE. No independent-corroboration mechanism is described; each Evidence Graph documents one result's own derivation, not agreement or disagreement across independently-arrived-at results.
memory_model: The Metadata Service (MongoDB for JSON-LD metadata) plus the graph store (Stardog) together function as persistent, queryable organizational memory for every object ever registered in a FAIRSCAPE instance -- durable and cross-session by construction (a 'data commons'), though scoped to computational-research objects rather than general agent/knowledge memory.
retrieval_context_model: Two explicit retrieval mechanisms: a literal-string Search Service over all object metadata, and the Evidence Graph Service's PID-rooted SPARQL PATH traversal (Materials and Methods) -- structural graph retrieval by identifier, not a relevance-ranked, dissent/authority-aware context-selection mechanism (H5 not matched).
decision_representation: NOT_APPLICABLE
requirement_derivation: NOT_APPLICABLE
specification_representation: NOT_APPLICABLE to software requirements; each microservice's interface is specified via OpenAPI/Swagger (Materials and Methods, per-service links), a software-interface specification, not a decision/requirement specification.
planning_model: NOT_APPLICABLE
execution_unit_session_model: The Compute Service treats one computation (a script/workflow/container run against PID-referenced inputs) as the execution unit, returning a job identifier and, on completion, automatically registering and PID-assigning all outputs with provenance metadata (Compute Service) -- a concrete, working execution-to-provenance-capture unit, though not phase- or context-bounded in the H8 sense (no notion of re-bounding a growing history).
artifact_code_linkage: Direct and strong: software, containers, and scripts are first-class registered objects with their own PIDs and metadata, resolvable and citable exactly like datasets (Abstract, 'persistent identifiers, including software'; Transfer Service) -- one of the more concrete artifact-linkage mechanisms found in this campaign.
test_verification_linkage: Framed as 'validation via inspection' rather than automated testing: the paper explicitly states that for very large analyses 'no reviewer will attempt to replicate such large-scale computations... The primary use case will be validation via inspection, and en passant validation via software reuse' (Introduction) -- a human-inspection verification model, not a test-suite or formal-verification linkage.
deployment_linkage: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS beyond FAIRSCAPE's own deployment flexibility (installable on private/public/hybrid cloud, bare-metal clusters, or laptops via minikube, Materials and Methods) -- this describes deploying FAIRSCAPE itself, not a linkage from a deployed artifact back to its originating evidence graph.
runtime_observation_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE beyond job-completion metadata capture at the Compute Service (job progress and completion are tracked, with outputs auto-registered); no linkage from post-deployment runtime telemetry back into the evidence graph is described.
feedback_to_knowledge_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE within this paper's own scope -- the Discussion frames evidence transparency as enabling future re-use, challenge, and debunking (citing the STAP stem-cell retraction as a cautionary example) but does not describe an automated mechanism by which a challenge or failed replication updates the evidence graph.
forward_traceability: Present: the Evidence Graph Service exposes 'all resources required to run a computation... by the evidence graph', enabling a user to 'reproduce the same computation by invoking the appropriate services... with the help of these identifiers' (Evidence Graph Service) -- forward from recorded provenance to re-executable computation.
backward_traceability: The paper's strongest, most concretely implemented mechanism: any citable object (dataset, image, figure, table) can have 'its complete evidence graph... retrieved as a validation of the object's derivation and as a set of URIs resolvable to reusable versions of the toolsets and data' (Introduction) -- full backward provenance from a published result to every dataset, software version, and computation step that produced it.
change_impact_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE as an implemented mechanism in this paper (see conflict_trust_mechanism -- challenge propagation is EVI's contribution, described here only as a design goal, not implemented/evaluated in this paper).
human_agent_scope: Human-centered: FAIRSCAPE is built for human computational scientists (data scientists, biomedical researchers) registering objects and running computations through a Python client or notebook UI; no autonomous agent participant is described (this is a 2021 paper, pre-dating LLM-agent memory systems) -- provenance/evidence exists to make HUMAN scientific claims transparent and reproducible, not to support agent reasoning.
implementation_availability: Yes, strongly -- a full production-grade, containerized (Kubernetes/Docker) microservices system with seven services (Transfer, Metadata, Object, Evidence Graph, Compute, Search, Visualization), publicly released on GitHub (github.com/fairscape/fairscape) and archived on Zenodo (Levinson et al., 2021), and deployed as a real data commons at the University of Virginia.
evaluation_method: Use-case demonstration rather than controlled experiment: the paper describes its deployment for large-scale neonatal/critical-care physiological signal analytics use cases at UVA (implied by author affiliations in Pediatrics/Medicine/Advanced Medical Analytics) rather than reporting a benchmark against alternative provenance systems; evaluation is qualitative (FAIR-principle compliance, architecture description) rather than quantitative.
strongest_dsystem_overlap: The most concretely OPERATIONALIZED evidence/provenance mechanism found in this campaign to date -- not a proposal but a real, running, publicly available system that automatically captures a complete, persistently-identified, machine-resolvable provenance graph (linking software, data, and computations) for every result, with strong artifact/software linkage and full backward traceability from a citable result to its derivation. This is the implementation substrate for the same EVI/evidence-graph mechanism already scored as a critical collision in this matrix's evidence-graphs-fair-computation-defeasible-reasoning-2021 row (same author group: Al Manir, Niestroy, Levinson, Clark).
strongest_difference: This paper's own novel contribution is infrastructural (microservices architecture, PID/ARK minting, authentication, storage-engine integration) rather than a new epistemic mechanism -- the defeasible-reasoning, challenge-propagation, and argumentation-theoretic apparatus that makes the evidence graph epistemically interesting (closest to H3/H10) is EVI's contribution, described here only as a design rationale, not implemented or evaluated in this paper. No decision, requirement, specification, planning, or agent-memory model is present at all; the scope is human-authored computational science, not agentic knowledge construction.
derivative_ancestor: evidence-graphs-fair-computation-defeasible-reasoning-2021 (Al Manir, Niestroy, Levinson, Clark -- already matrixed as a critical collision). Same author group (three of four authors overlap, with Timothy Clark as corresponding/senior author on both); FAIRSCAPE explicitly states it implements 'the EVI ontology (Al Manir et al., 2021a, 2021b)' and abstracted its evidence-graph model from the authors' own prior Micropublications work (Clark et al., 2014). This is the implementation/infrastructure paper for the same mechanism already captured by the ancestor row, not an independent invention -- consistent with the coordinator's framing of this source as 'implementation substrate for the same evidence/provenance mechanism.'
evidence_locator: PMC open-access full text (CC-BY 4.0, PMCID PMC8760356, pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8760356/; matches the published Neuroinformatics 20(1):187-202 record): Abstract; Introduction/Motivation (evidence graphs as directed acyclic support graphs, argumentation-theoretic basis); Related Work (EVI ontology, W3C PROV, Al Manir et al. 2021a/2021b citation); 'Enabling Transparency through EVI's Formal Model' section (defeasible claims, challenge propagation); Materials and Methods (architectural layers, seven microservices: Transfer, Metadata, Object, Evidence Graph, Compute, Search, Visualization; ARK PIDs); Discussion (virtual witnessing, STAP retraction example); Conclusion.
verbatim_notes: "FAIRSCAPE fully implements the FAIR data principles and extends them to provide fully FAIR Evidence, including machine-interpretable provenance of datasets, software and computations, as metadata for all computed results" (Abstract). "EVI is based on the fundamental idea that scientific findings or claims are not facts, but assertions backed by some level of evidence, i.e., they are defeasible components of argumentation" (Enabling Transparency through EVI's Formal Model). "the complete evidence graph may be retrieved as a validation of the object's derivation and as a set of URIs resolvable to reusable versions of the toolsets and data" (Introduction).

citation: Bara, M.: Epistemic Sybil Resistance: Multiplying AI Agents Without Multiplying Evidence, arXiv preprint, 1 Sep 2026
problem_addressed: Multiple AI agents spawned from identical or overlapping evidence sources produce apparently independent reports that are actually derived from shared roots; naive aggregation (e.g. counting reports) overcounts evidence and yields overconfident posteriors. The paper formalizes when an additional report contributes zero new information given already-admitted reports (an "epistemic Sybil extension").
state_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- the paper has no ontological/epistemic/lifecycle state model for knowledge items; its unit of analysis is a report Z about a latent true state Theta, not a persistent knowledge-graph node.
transition_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no typed append-only transition log; the model is an admission decision over a profile of reports R, not a state-transition system.
provenance_model: Central contribution (Sec.6, "Provenance as Side Information"): an explicit provenance graph G=(V,E_G), a DAG whose nodes represent primitive observations, datasets, documents, transformations, retrieval operations, models, agents, and reports, and whose edges u->v record that information from u was available in generating v; root sets R(R_i) denote each report's authenticated primitive roots, exposed via a side-information interface J with authenticated provenance J_G.
actor_model: Reports are attributed to agents/extractors in the graph's node types, but there is no actor-authority, delegation, or human-actor model -- Sec.8's empirical study uses a single LLM (Haiku-class) as the sole extractor across all agent instances, so "actor" reduces to "which copy of the same extractor produced this report."
temporal_model: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS -- no explicit valid-time/transaction-time or bitemporal treatment found in the sections read; Theta is treated as a fixed latent parameter, not an evolving one.
conflict_trust_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- the paper addresses over-counting of agreeing evidence, not resolution of conflicting/contradictory claims; disagreement between reports is out of scope.
convergence_independence_mechanism: Core mechanism, and the closest primary-source match found in this campaign for H4: the epistemic-Sybil test I(Theta;Z|R)=0 identifies when a new report adds zero conditional information given admitted reports; Corollary 2 (Sec.5.2) derives kappa_m = 1/(1+rho(m-1)) = m_eff/m for m equicorrelated reports sharing one Gaussian-modeled root, formalizing "derivative agreement is discounted" quantitatively; Sec.5.3 shows correlated extraction errors from a shared base model impose an information ceiling agent multiplicity cannot remove (gamma=0.719 empirical fit).
memory_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not a memory architecture; a formal aggregation-rule specification consumed at inference time, not a persistent store.
retrieval_context_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no retrieval or context-selection mechanism is proposed; the paper specifies what an aggregator should condition on, not how to retrieve it.
decision_representation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed.
requirement_derivation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed.
specification_representation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed.
planning_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed.
execution_unit_session_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed; Sec.8's 20,000+ LLM calls are an evaluation harness, not a session/phase abstraction.
artifact_code_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed.
test_verification_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed (Monte Carlo simulation and the LLM extraction study in Secs.7-8 validate the formal model itself, not a software artifact).
deployment_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed.
runtime_observation_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed.
feedback_to_knowledge_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed.
forward_traceability: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed.
backward_traceability: Partial and central to the mechanism: every report Z's admission decision requires tracing back through the provenance DAG to its authenticated root set R(Z) so shared ancestry with already-admitted reports R can be detected -- a narrow, single-purpose backward trace (report -> evidentiary roots), not D-System's general artifact-to-reasoning backward trace.
change_impact_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed; no notion of retracting or falsifying an assumption and propagating that change.
human_agent_scope: AI-agent-only. Section 8's related-work framing cites epistemology and jury/testimony literature for conceptual grounding, but no human witnesses, judges, or mixed human-AI evidence are modeled or evaluated; explicitly outside H4's "mixed human-agent knowledge" scope.

problem_addressed: Production LLM-agent memory systems apply one of four ad hoc contradiction-resolution heuristics (last-writer-wins, evidence-weighted merge, await-confirmation, per-rule policy) without declaring the isolation level assumed or the write-time anomalies admitted; the paper treats contradiction resolution as write-time concurrency control and supplies the missing formal contract (Abstract; Sec.1).
state_model: No ontological-type or lifecycle-classification axis is defined anywhere in the paper (confirmed on full-text read). The formal state is a dual-row bitemporal schema (Table 2, Sec.3.1): eleven user-visible columns (fact_id, subject, predicate, object, valid_from, valid_to, system_time_start, system_time_end, provenance_id, confidence, resolution_strategy_id) plus a hidden row_kind discriminator in {current, audit}. Valid-time/system-time are temporal dimensions, not lifecycle stages; there is no axis classifying what kind of thing a fact is and no lifecycle-stage enumeration (draft/active/superseded/archived) -- confirmed absent, not merely undiscussed.
transition_model: Four named heuristics (last-writer-wins, evidence-weighted merge, await-confirmation, per-rule policy) are typed as one family of bitemporal operators (Sec.3.2); each operator carries an isolation precondition and emits an audit row on the losing fact via Audit=(pw XOR pl, strat, ts) (Sec.3.2). This is a typed operator family over write-time concurrency phenomena, not D-System's S_t--[T,P]-->S_t+1 transition on a classified knowledge state -- the operators act on facts under isolation/schema/provenance preconditions, not on ontological/epistemic/lifecycle-classified states.
provenance_model: Each tuple carries an element of a commutative semiring P=<K,+,*,0,1> (Sec.2.2); provenance is 'a two-sort polynomial W in K[X,T]' (Sec.2.2), and the audit row preserves the losing fact's provenance under Theorem 7's 'audit-erasure schema lift' (Sec.3.3). This is a mathematically rich provenance model but the paper does not instantiate K with actor identity, domain authority, method or delegation -- it is left abstract for a deployment to fill in.
actor_model: No human-actor or authority-delegation model. The only named actor-like entity is 'the adjudicating judge' -- an LLM or content-addressed comparator kept on or off the write path (Sec.4.6 verdict matrix); the tightness companion proves 'keyed logging of the adjudicating judge is necessary for replay consistency' (Abstract). No multi-human, multi-agent, or authority-hierarchy model is defined.
temporal_model: Full bitemporal model: separate valid-time (valid_from/valid_to) and system-time (system_time_start/system_time_end) columns (Table 2, Sec.3.1), in the Snodgrass bitemporal-database tradition (cited Sec.5; see derivative_ancestor). Genuine, formally specified, and more explicit than D-System's single TemporalScope field, though scoped to fact validity/audit rather than knowledge-state lifecycle.
conflict_trust_mechanism: Central contract: the four production heuristics are typed against an isolation lattice L_iso={RC<=SI<=SR} (Sec.2.2, 3.3) and soundness is proved by four theorems (Theorems 3, 7, 11, 12, Sec.3.3) closing the contract across isolation, schema and provenance. A verdict matrix over eight systems (Sec.4.1, 4.6) shows every baseline keeping a judge on the write path admits at least one of three write-time anomalies (replay inconsistency N1, belief-drift skew N2, audit erasure N3); TOKI alone excludes all three while keeping the judge (Abstract).

memory_model: LLM-agent persistent memory as a write-heavy substrate (Abstract); the dual-row bitemporal schema (Sec.3.1) is the storage model, with a reproducibility artifact and reference implementation released (Comments field; github.com/ZenAlexa/toki-bitemporal-memory).

No formal p-values reported in the sections read; 'joint family-wise robustness across every paired-accuracy test' is the closest statistical-rigor statement found (Appendix E.1).

citation: sciganec: subit-wiki -- SUBIT: Epistemic State Machine with Self-Evolving Ontology, GitHub repository
problem_addressed: Classifying arbitrary text/knowledge blocks into a discrete epistemic-state space and inferring the most probable trajectory of state transitions across a document/corpus, so a wiki-like knowledge base can be organized by who is speaking, in what direction, and at what stage of maturity, rather than by topic alone (schema/subit-schema.md; README pipeline: text -> embedding -> P(sigma|s) -> Viterbi -> sigma* trajectory).
state_model: A fixed 64-state space (schema/subit-schema.md, read in full) built from three independent 2-bit axes, combinatorially: WHO (ME|WE|YOU|THEY -- subjectivity/perspective), WHERE (EAST|SOUTH|WEST|NORTH -- 'direction/intention in knowledge space': genesis/development/analysis/synthesis), WHEN (SPRING|SUMMER|AUTUMN|WINTER -- 'epistemic phase': nascent/active/evaluative/archived-concluded). code = (WHO<<4)|(WHERE<<2)|WHEN. citation: Barakat, L., Taylor, P., Griffiths, N., Miles, S. "Corroboration via Provenance Patterns." Proceedings of the 9th USENIX Workshop on the Theory and Practice of Provenance (TaPP 2017), Seattle, WA, June 22-23, 2017.
problem_addressed: Verifying the truthfulness of a provenance claim made by an autonomous, self-interested provenance source ("computational or human") by seeking corroborating evidence in the PROV reports of other sources, so that a self-interested source cannot freely misreport events (e.g. falsely blaming a "freak event" for poor service performance) to protect its own interests.
state_model: A claim = (M, W): a main part M (the core assertion) plus a context part W (supplementary clauses identifying relevant witnesses); clauses are typed rel(c1,c2) over PROV nodes/attributes within a concept-type lattice T = Te u Ta u Tg u Tp (Sec.2). No ontological+epistemic+lifecycle (O,E,L) state triple; no persistent knowledge-state object beyond the claim/report structure itself.
transition_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no typed S_t->S_t+1 transition model. The paper instead models abstraction operations on a claim (claim --op--> claim_i via individual generalisation / concept-type generalisation / clause detachment, Sec.3.1) as a recall-widening search technique with an associated information-loss uncertainty (Eq.2), not a knowledge-state transition with provenance-typed edges.
provenance_model: Standard W3C PROV (entity/activity/agent; wasGeneratedBy/used/wasAssociatedWith/actedOnBehalfOf; Fig.1) extended with the concept-type lattice T and relationship set R (Sec.2). Claims are PROV sub-graphs; witness patterns (ptrn_W) and confirmation patterns (ptrn_M+W) are abstracted PROV graphs matched against other sources' reports via a formally defined graph-projection satisfaction relation rprt=>ptrn (Sec.3.2, Definition, three numbered conditions).
actor_model: Provenance "sources" = PROV agents, explicitly scoped in the Abstract as "computational or human"; Sec.1 calls them "system members," modeled as autonomous, self-interested, and potentially untruthful ("may claim untrue data to protect their interests"). No delegation/domain-authority model beyond PROV's actedOnBehalfOf; no differential treatment of human vs. computational witnesses anywhere in the methodology.
temporal_model: Claims carry PROV timestamps (startTime/endTime, Fig.3) usable as context clauses for witness relevance (e.g. "providers relevant... around time frame [time1,time2]"); no bitemporal (valid-time vs. system-time) distinction.
conflict_trust_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE as a distinct mechanism -- the paper computes a single claim's reliability score against corroborating/non-corroborating witnesses (Eq.1); it does not model conflicting claims between sources or arbitrate between them.
convergence_independence_mechanism: Eq.1 (Sec.3): rel(claim) = |S_M+W| / |S_W| -- ratio of confirming relevant witnesses to total relevant witnesses, explicitly built on an assumed-independent-witness model. Sec.5 (Discussion and Related Work) states: "When estimating the reliability score of a claim (Equation 1), we have assumed independence among witnesses," flags that witnesses may share dependencies ("two different providers might outsource their sub-tasks to the same sub-providers... making their experiences similar and thus their testimonies redundant"), and sketches -- without implementing -- a reweighted Eq.8: rel(claim) = [sum_{s in S_M+W} weight(s)] / [sum_{s in S_W} weight(s)], analogized explicitly to "the channel weighting for a multi-version fault tolerant system (Townend et al. 2005)." problem_addressed: Representing "knowledge provenance" -- the provenance of a scientific assertion derived not from one publication/source but from an aggregation of multiple sources with potentially supporting and conflicting evidence -- as a fourth component on top of the standard three-part nanopublication model (assertion/provenance/publication-info graphs), applied at scale to 197,511 automatically-extracted gene expression-cancer facts (CoreKB, built by the CORE system).
state_model: A Proposition ("the smallest piece of information to which provenance-related attributes may be ascribed... a declarative sentence that is either true or false") carries an AssignedTruthValue (creator-assigned) and TrustedTruthValue (evaluator-assigned), each with a certainty degree (probability, xsd:float) and prov:atTime timestamp; a Proposition is further classified ReliableFact or UnreliableFact (subclassed InsufficientEvidence / ContrastingEvidence) via threshold tests. A truth-value classification, not D-System's orthogonal ontological+epistemic+lifecycle (O,E,L) state triple.
transition_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no typed S_t->S_t+1 transition is modeled. Truth values carry a single timestamp marking when a value was assigned/trusted; no append-only transition history or edge-typed evolution between states is described.
provenance_model: PROV-K ontology (Fig.1), extending PROV-O: Proposition (subclass of prov:Entity) linked via supportedBy/conflictingWith (range class Sentence, from the Semanticscience Integrated Ontology) to supporting/conflicting evidence sentences; Document/dc:creator/prov:wasDerivedFrom for source documents; a Signature class for digital-signature status. Implemented as the 4th named graph ("knowledgeProv") of an extended nanopublication, alongside the standard assertion/provenance/publicationInfo graphs, backward-compatible with the original 3-graph nanopublication model.
actor_model: Two trust relationships (Fig.1/2): InfoCreatorTrust ("the provenance requester a 'trusts' information creator c in a specific knowledge field f") between two prov:Agents, and PropositionTrust ("Proposition x is trusted by an agent a") between an agent and a proposition. In the real-world CoreKB deployment all propositions are machine-generated ("Automatic Assertion") and all evidence is machine-extracted literature sentences ("Combinatorial Evidence") -- no human witness participates in the deployed system, though the ontology's Agent class is generic (prov:Agent, "a person or a digital artifact") and not restricted by the ontology definition itself.
temporal_model: prov:atTime timestamps on truth-value assignment/trust events only; no bitemporal (valid-time vs. system-time) model.
conflict_trust_mechanism: A two-stage threshold test (CoreKB case study, Sec.4): (1) sufficiency criteria -- Change-of-Cancer-Status and Gene-Cancer-Interaction probabilities must not be below informativeness threshold alpha=0.7; (2) consistency criteria -- the probability gap between the two most likely gene classes must exceed threshold beta=0.4. A Proposition failing either test becomes UnreliableFact (InsufficientEvidence or ContrastingEvidence) with a recorded unreliabilityReason/unmetCondition. Threshold-based sufficiency/consistency arbitration over supporting-vs-conflicting evidence counts, not a graph-topology or lineage-based discount.
convergence_independence_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE / absent as a topology-aware mechanism -- searched for specifically per this dispatch's H4 mandate and not found. The knowledgeProv graph records which Sentences supportedBy vs conflictingWith a Proposition (worked example, Fig.3/4: 83 supporting, 41 conflicting, certainty degree 0.81542736) and the sufficiency/consistency thresholds act on the resulting probability distribution, but nothing discounts a supporting sentence's contribution for sharing lineage or dependence with another supporting sentence (e.g. the same underlying study). Naive support/conflict counting into a probability -- the same shape of mechanism the campaign's existing dong-2009 negative finding describes for H4, not a shared-ancestry discount.

implementation_availability: Deployed and published at scale: 197,511 extended nanopublications (156,172 ReliableFact + 41,339 ContrastingEvidence, Table 1) serialized from CoreKB, browsable/downloadable on the CoreKB platform and archived in bulk on Zenodo [14]; PROV-K ontology publicly available (prov-k.dei.unipd.it/ontology/); source code for building extended nanopublications released on GitHub (github.com/mntlra/knowledgeProvenance) -- a real, large-scale, running system, not a toy example.
evaluation_method: NOT_APPLICABLE as a comparative/benchmark evaluation of the knowledge-provenance extension itself -- no precision/recall/accuracy figures are reported for the extension; Table 1 reports only descriptive counts (gene-class distribution across the 197,511 published nanopublications). The underlying CORE extraction system's own accuracy is evaluated in a separate cited paper [9], out of this paper's scope.
strongest_dsystem_overlap: A real, deployed, large-scale (197K+ facts) provenance/trust/reliability ontology (PROV-K, extending PROV-O) linking a claim (Proposition) to multiple supporting and conflicting evidence sources with an assigned certainty degree and a threshold-based reliability classification (ReliableFact/UnreliableFact) -- genuine multi-source claim/provenance/trust architecture, closer to D-System's H3 (provenance as conflict-resolution input) territory than H4's independence-discount claim.
strongest_difference: No independence-aware or shared-lineage discount mechanism exists anywhere in the paper -- searched for specifically and not found. Reliability rests entirely on sufficiency/consistency probability thresholds over supporting-vs-conflicting sentence counts (naive counting), with no treatment of whether two supporting sentences might share a dependent origin, unlike barakat-corroboration-provenance-patterns-tapp2017 (this dispatch, rank 1), which at least names shared-dependency discounting as an open problem. The human/computational scope question this dispatch's own prior search (LIT-08-S046) flagged as inferred-not-confirmed is now confirmed negatively by direct reading: the paper's one real-world deployment (CoreKB) is end-to-end automated, not mixed human-agent.
derivative_ancestor: none for an H4-specific mechanism, since no such mechanism exists in this source to have an ancestor.
